76.title: Emergency Passport - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
76.text: Emergency Passport - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco. The emergency passport is a non-biometric, machine-readable passport. Its validity cannot exceed one (01) year. It is issued in extremely urgent cases and on an exceptional basis to: (1) unregistered citizens who need a valid passport to regularize their immigration status; (2) registered citizens from another country whose passport was lost, damaged or stolen while in the USA; (3) registered citizens without a US passport who lack a biometric electronic passport and must travel urgently for family, professional, administrative or health reasons; (4) Algerian citizens temporarily abroad whose passport was lost, damaged or stolen and who must travel to one or more foreign countries before returning to Algeria. Required documents: 1. A written request to the Consul General explaining the purpose of the application. 2. Emergency passport application form, completed and signed by the applicant. 3. Proof of Algerian nationality (old passport, consular card, or identity card). 4. Proof of address. 5. Documents proving the emergency. 6. Two (2) current passport photos with a plain white background. 7.

77.title: Emergency Passport - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
77.text: of Algerian nationality (old passport, consular card, or identity card). 4. Proof of address. 5. Documents proving the emergency. 6. Two (2) current passport photos with a plain white background. 7. A $75 USD USPS money order. For a faster and safer return of your documents, provide a Priority Mail Express return envelope. No processing time stated.

78.title: Travel Documents (Laissez-passer) - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
78.text: Laissez-passer - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco. The laissez-passer is a one-way travel document for Algerian nationals whose passports are lost, stolen or expired, and for newborns of Algerian parents in the USA who are visiting or lack legal status. Valid for 30 days, for a return to Algeria by the shortest route. The request must be submitted at the latest 72 hours before the departure date. Adults: Laissez-passer Application Form duly filled out and signed; two (02) recent photographs; proof of Algerian nationality (passport, Algerian national identity card, consular card, or military card); the damaged or expired Algerian passport, or a copy in case of loss; a declaration of theft/loss issued by the Police Department; one way flight ticket; Priority Mail Express return envelope.

79.title: Travel Documents (Laissez-passer) - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
79.text: card); the damaged or expired Algerian passport, or a copy in case of loss; a declaration of theft/loss issued by the Police Department; one way flight ticket; Priority Mail Express return envelope. Minors or newborns: Laissez-passer Application Form duly filled out and signed; two (02) recent photographs; proof of the parent's Algerian nationality (passport, national identity card, consular card, or military card); the original Birth Certificate of the child (Full version); the damaged or expired Algerian passport, or a copy in case of loss; a declaration of theft/loss issued by the Police Department; if the father is Algerian, his authorization, legalized by a US notary, or by an administrative officer in Algeria; Priority Mail Express return envelope. No fee or payment method is stated on the page.

80.title: First-Time Registration - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
80.text: Consular Registration (First-Time) - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco. Algerian citizens living abroad permanently who are 19 or older must complete consular registration to obtain passports and ID documents. A married woman can be registered under her husband's file; children under 19 are registered with their parents. Registration includes a consular card issued free of charge, valid for five years. Documents can be submitted in person or by mail to the Consulate General, 465 California St., Suite 900, San Francisco, CA 94104. Required documents: completed and signed application form; two recent passport photos, 2x2 inches (51x51 mm); original full-size birth certificate (E.C 12, full copy) if born in Algeria, or any birth certificate if born abroad; a parent's birth certificate or Algerian nationality certificate (not required if the parent holds a consular card); for applicants born overseas, either a nationality certificate or the birth certificates of two male ascendants born in Algeria; copy of the photo page of the Algerian passport, if available; copy of US entry visa; copy of proof of legal US stay (US passport, naturalization certificate, green card,

81.title: First-Time Registration - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
81.text: ascendants born in Algeria; copy of the photo page of the Algerian passport, if available; copy of US entry visa; copy of proof of legal US stay (US passport, naturalization certificate, green card, nonimmigrant visa, or a USCIS document); Algerian marriage certificate, family book, divorce certificate or decree, or spouse's death certificate, if applicable; proof of employment, self-employment, or school enrollment (alternatives accepted); proof of US address (utility bill, lease agreement, etc.); self-addressed stamped envelope.

82.title: Registration Renewal - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
82.text: Consular Registration Renewal - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco. Required documents: completed and signed application form; two recent standard photos; expired consular card (if available); copy of proof of lawful stay in the US (US passport, naturalization certificate, green card, nonimmigrant visa, or a USCIS document); if applicable, copy of Algerian marriage certificate, family book, divorce certificate or decree, or spouse's death certificate; proof of employment, self-employment, or school enrollment (if different from the initial registration); proof of US address (utility bill, lease agreement); self-addressed stamped envelope. No fee stated (consular card is free per the first-registration page).

83.title: Transfer of File - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
83.text: Transfer of Consular File - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco. The Consulate carries out this procedure; registration is granted as soon as the file is received from the previous Embassy/Consulate. Required documents: 1. Application form, completed and signed. 2. Two recent passport photos, 2x2 inches (51x51 mm). 3. Original full-size birth certificate ('Copie integrale', E.C 12) if born in Algeria, or any birth certificate if born abroad. 4. Copy of the photo page of your Algerian passport, if available. 5. Copy of US entry visa. 6. Copy of proof of legal US stay (US passport, naturalization certificate, green card, nonimmigrant visa, or USCIS document). 7. Copy of Algerian marriage certificate, family book, divorce certificate or decree, or spouse's death certificate, if applicable. 8. Proof of employment, self-employment, or school enrollment (alternatives accepted). 9. Proof of U.S. address (utility bill, lease agreement). 10. Self-addressed stamped envelope.

84.title: Cancellation of Registration - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
84.text: Cancellation of Consular Registration - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco. Required documents: application form, completed and signed by the applicant; original consular card; a USPS money order for $2.50; a self-addressed stamped envelope. If the applicant is in Algeria, the cancellation request ('radiation' / shatb) can be submitted in person at the Civil Status Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and National Community Abroad, Plateau des Annassers, Kouba, Algiers.

85.title: Births - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
85.text: Births (Birth Transcription) - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco. Algerian parents are expected to register their child's birth. The 12-S (extract of birth certificate) is needed for passport and/or ID card applications. Applications can be submitted in person or by mail; mailed applications should include a USPS Priority Mail return envelope. Born in the USA (19 states of jurisdiction): the parents' first and last names on the child's birth certificate must match the Algerian Civil Status register; completed and signed application form; original or certified copy of the full birth certificate from the city hall, including the time of birth (returned after verification and certification); copy of the applicant's or a parent's proof of Algerian nationality and identity (passport, national ID, consular card, or military card); Family Book, if available; for mailed applications, a Priority Mail return envelope.

86.title: Births - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
86.text: a parent's proof of Algerian nationality and identity (passport, national ID, consular card, or military card); Family Book, if available; for mailed applications, a Priority Mail return envelope. Born in another country: same name-matching requirement; completed and signed application form; original or certified copy of the full birth certificate issued by the country of birth (returned after verification); copy of the applicant's or parent's proof of Algerian nationality and identity; Family Book, if available; Priority Mail return envelope for mailed applications. No fees or processing times stated.

87.title: Marriages - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
87.text: Marriages (Marriage Transcription and Family Book) - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco. Marriages in the United States involving an Algerian national can be registered at the Consulate General. A family book (livret de famille) is issued after registration, free of charge. Applications can be filed in person or by mail; mailed applications should include a USPS Priority Mail return envelope. Algerian couple: names on the marriage certificate must match the Algerian Civil Status register; completed and signed Descriptive Form; original American marriage certificate (returned after verification and certification); copy of proof of Algerian nationality and identity (passport, National ID, Consular card, or Military card); original birth certificates of both spouses issued within the last three months (returned after verification); Priority Mail return envelope if by mail.

88.title: Marriages - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
88.text: ID, Consular card, or Military card); original birth certificates of both spouses issued within the last three months (returned after verification); Priority Mail return envelope if by mail. Non-Algerian husband (Algerian wife): same as above, with a copy of the wife's proof of Algerian nationality; original birth certificates of both spouses (the Algerian national's issued within the last three months); if the husband was born non-Muslim, a certificate of conversion to Islam issued by a mosque or an agreed association. Non-Algerian wife (Algerian husband): same as above, with a copy of the husband's proof of Algerian nationality; original birth certificates of both spouses (the Algerian national's issued within the last three months). No other fees or processing times stated.

89.title: Deaths - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
89.text: Deaths (Death Report and Repatriation of Remains) - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco. Body transfer to Algeria: the Consulate General guides and assists relatives with the administrative steps; paperwork will be dealt with by the Funeral Services appointed by the deceased's family or relatives. The Consulate General issues the Algerian death certificate (after transcription) and the transfer authorization (Autorisation de Transfert de corps). Documents: 1. names of the deceased and parents on the US death certificate must match the Algerian Civil Status register; 2. completed and signed Death Report; 3. original US death certificate (returned after verification and certification); 4. birth certificate of the deceased; 5. copy of proof of Algerian nationality and identity (passport, national ID, consular card, or military card); 6. Family Book, if available; 7. medical letter from the Department of Health stating the death was not from an infectious or communicable disease; 8. embalming certificate from the funeral services; 9. transit permit from City Hall; 10. certificate stating the body was laid out according to Muslim rituals; 11. airway bill (flight itinerary).

90.title: Deaths - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
90.text: 8. embalming certificate from the funeral services; 9. transit permit from City Hall; 10. certificate stating the body was laid out according to Muslim rituals; 11. airway bill (flight itinerary). Death Report only: name-matching confirmation; completed and signed Death Report; birth certificate of the deceased; original US death certificate (returned after verification); copy of proof of Algerian nationality and identity; Family Book, if available. If by mail, include a USPS Priority Mail return envelope. No fees stated.

91.title: Power of Attorney - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
91.text: Power of Attorney (Procuration) - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco. A power of attorney is a legal document that appoints someone (procurator) to manage your personal or business affairs on your behalf; you can define and limit that person's authority. The service is offered exclusively to Algerian citizens without a prior appointment, for use in Algeria. Apply by mail to the Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco, 465 California St., Suite 900, San Francisco, CA 94104. Required documents: 1. proxy form, signed and notarized by a public notary; 2. notarized copy of your Algerian passport (main page), Algerian ID card, or military card; 3. USPS money order for $6.25 per proxy; 4. optional (recommended) USPS Priority Mail return envelope.

92.title: Translation - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
92.text: Translation Services - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco. Civil status documents: the Consulate can translate Algerian civil status certificates (marriage, birth, death) into English. Required: the original Algerian document; a USPS money order for two dollars and fifty cents ($2.5); a prepaid self-addressed return envelope. Other documents: the Consulate can translate Algerian driving licenses, ID cards and military cards into English. Required: the original and a copy of the document to be translated; a USPS money order for $2.5; a USPS Priority Mail return envelope.

93.title: Census (between 17 and 18 years old) - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
93.text: National Service Census - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco. Census of the 2029 national service class: Algerian citizens born between January 1 and December 31, 2009 residing in the consular jurisdiction of the Consulate General in San Francisco must submit documents to the Consulate General before October 1, 2026. Documents: enrollment form, completed electronically on screen and then hand-signed by the legal guardian; one original Algerian birth certificate; two recent ID photos; copy of the legal guardian's consular card; a self-addressed stamped envelope for mailing the census certificate. No fees stated.

94.title: Deferment - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
94.text: National Service Deferment (Sursis) - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco. Required documents: 1. original previous deferment document (for renewal); 2. copy of consular registration card; 3. application form completed electronically on screen; 4. two recent passport photos 2x2 inches (51x51 mm); 5. one original Algerian birth certificate ('12S are not accepted'); 6. copy of school transcript, proof of enrollment, or last school diploma or certificate ('School IDs are not accepted'). Optional: prepaid USPS Priority return envelope. No fees stated.

95.title: Visa Procedure - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
95.text: Visa Procedure - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco. The Consulate General handles visa applications from residents of its consular jurisdiction (19 US states). The application form must be filled out electronically, clear and accurate, with photos attached as indicated. Applicants are urged to apply sixty (60) days before travel. Processing times vary by visa type and bilateral agreements; in-person or mailed applications are generally issued within a week of receipt. The Consulate General may request additional documents. Submitting the required documents does not guarantee a visa. Mail applications to: Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco, 465 California St., Suite 900, San Francisco, CA 94104.

96.title: Tourist Visa - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
96.text: Tourist Visa - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco. Requirements: 1. application form filled out on-screen, printed, dated and hand signed; 2. one recent standard photo; 3. one of: confirmed hotel reservation; holiday booking through a travel agency; invitation letter from a resident of Algeria notarized by an Algerian city hall with the host's Algerian ID attached; or invitation letter from an Algerian host who is a US resident issued at a public notary office (in either invitation case the Algerian host must be registered with the Consulate General in San Francisco); 4. copy of airline itinerary; 5. most recent statement of financial resources or proof of income (pay stub, bank statement); 6. original passport and copy of main photo page, valid at least 6 months with at least two blank pages; 7. for non-US passports, copy of US legal residency (Green Card or appropriate visa); 8. proof of address within the consular jurisdiction (driver's license, utility bill, bank or credit card statement, insurance policy or bill); 9. optional Priority Mail Express return envelope. Fee: US passports $160 (non-refundable); other passports per a separate fee list (not retrieved).

97.title: Tourist Visa - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
97.text: credit card statement, insurance policy or bill); 9. optional Priority Mail Express return envelope. Fee: US passports $160 (non-refundable); other passports per a separate fee list (not retrieved). Payment by USPS money order.

98.title: Family Visa - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
98.text: Family Visa - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco. Issued to members of an Algerian family who is registered at the Consulate General. Required: 1. visa application form completed on-screen, printed, dated, hand-signed; 2. one recent standard photo; 3. copy of the Algerian relative's consular card; 4. copy of proof of relationship (marriage or birth certificate); 5. original passport and copy of main photo page, valid at least six months with at least two blank pages; 6. for non-US passports, copy of US legal residency document (Green Card or appropriate visa); 7. proof of residence within the consulate's jurisdiction (driver's license, utility bill, bank or credit card statement, insurance policy or bill); 8. USPS Priority Mail return envelope (recommended). Fee: 'The visa fee for US passports is 160$ (Non-refundable).' Other passports per a separate fee list (not retrieved). Payment by USPS money order.

99.title: Transit Visa - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
99.text: Transit Visa - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco. Issued to people transiting through the Algerian territory who hold an entry visa for their destination country. Maximum duration: 7 days. Required: application form completed on-screen, printed, dated, hand-signed; one recent standard photo; hotel reservation; copy of airline itinerary; most recent statement of financial resources or proof of income; original passport and copy of main photo page (valid at least 6 months, at least two blank pages); for non-US passports, copy of US legal residency document; proof of address within the consular jurisdiction; optional Priority Mail Express return envelope. Fee: US passports $160 (non-refundable); other passports per separate list. Payment by USPS money order.

100.title: Regularization of the Situation of Algerian Citizens Residing Abroad - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
100.text: Regularization announcement - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco. The Consulate General informs Algerian nationals in its consular jurisdiction about exceptional measures, announced under a decision of President Abdelmadjid Tebboune, allowing Algerian citizens abroad in vulnerable or irregular situations who face judicial or administrative proceedings (notably young people facing proceedings for misdemeanors affecting public order) to regularize their legal status. To apply: contact the consular service, submit the approved form ('Regularization_Request_Form') and the required supporting documents. The Consulate will support applicants and track requests until a final decision is issued. No deadlines or fees stated.

101.title: Jurisdiction - Consular Coverage (Embassy of Algeria in Washington) - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
101.text: Algerian consular jurisdiction in the United States (Embassy of Algeria in Washington page). Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco (19 states): California, Arizona, Nevada, Oregon, Washington, Utah, Colorado, Hawaii, Alaska, North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, Oklahoma, Texas, Kansas, Wyoming, Montana, Idaho, New Mexico. Consulate General of Algeria in New York (25 states): Alabama, Arkansas, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Vermont, Wisconsin. Embassy of Algeria in Washington, D.C.: Delaware, Maryland, North Carolina, South Carolina, Virginia, West Virginia, Washington D.C. San Francisco consulate address (from its service pages): 465 California St., Suite 900, San Francisco, CA 94104. Email (passport status help): secretariat@cgalgeriasf.org.

102.title: Mobile Station to Chicago 2023 - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
102.text: Announcement - Consulate General of Algeria in New York (cgnewyork.mfa.gov.dz). The Consulate General planned a mobile biometric station in Chicago in 2023 for photo and fingerprint taking for biometric passports, the only procedure requiring in-person appearance (applicants over 12). Registered nationals whose passports had expired or would be invalid by November 15, 2023 had to mail their files to the Consulate before May 8, 2023. Passport, registration renewal and first registration applications could be sent together. Fingerprinting in Chicago was only possible if the application had already been sent to the New York Consulate. 'NO OTHER SERVICE SUCH AS VISA, REGISTRATION, PROXY ETC.. WILL BE GRANTED.' Contact: ms@algeria-cgny.org. Hours stated on the site: all consular services except visas, Tuesday to Saturday 9 am to 3 pm (Saturday 9 am to 2:30 pm); visa lodging Tuesday to Friday 9 am to 12 pm. (Historical 2023 announcement.)

103.title: Biometric Passport - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
103.text: Biometric Passport - Consulate General of Algeria in New York. Biometric passports are issued to Algerian citizens living abroad permanently, after their consular registration is finalized. Start renewal about six months before the current passport expires. Passports are issued in Algeria, so there is usually a delay of several weeks. Track status with the number on your receipt about one week after fingerprint/photo/signature capture on the Algerian Ministry of the Interior passport tracking site. Passport services require an appointment; all other consular services are available without one. Under 12: no fingerprinting or in-person pickup needed; send all documents by mail. 12 and older: must appear in person for fingerprinting; sending the application by mail before attending is recommended. First-time: passport form completed and signed (by legal tutor for minors); two 2x2 inch (51x51 mm) recent photos, white background, neutral expression, no smile, clear forehead; original 12-S birth certificate; copy of proof of US residency (US passport, Green Card, US birth certificate, or appropriate visa); USPS Priority Mail return envelope.

104.title: Biometric Passport - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
104.text: no smile, clear forehead; original 12-S birth certificate; copy of proof of US residency (US passport, Green Card, US birth certificate, or appropriate visa); USPS Priority Mail return envelope. Renewal: passport renewal form completed and signed (by legal tutor for minors); two 2x2 photos; original 12-S birth certificate only if the old biometric passport was not issued by the Consulate General in New York; copy of proof of US residency; USPS Priority Mail return envelope. Book options: Standard (28 pages) or Large (48 pages). Fees by USPS money order. Standard fees per the official fee page: students and children under 19 - $37.50 (28 pages), $56.25 (48 pages); employed or unemployed - $75.00 (28 pages), $112.50 (48 pages). The passport page also lists 'passport and penalty fees' for lost, stolen, damaged or late renewal: $100, $118.75, $200, $237.50 (category mapping not explicit on the page; confirm with the consulate).

105.title: Emergency Passport - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
105.text: Emergency Passport - Consulate General of Algeria in New York. The emergency passport is a non-biometric, machine-readable passport printed at Algerian embassies and consulates and, in some cases, by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Algiers. Its validity is non-extendable and ranges from 3 months to one year depending on purpose. A. Issued by the Consulate General: 1. written request to the Consul General explaining the need; 2. emergency passport application form, completed and signed; 3. proof of Algerian nationality (old passport, consular card, or identity card); 4. proof of address in the consulate's states of jurisdiction; 5. proof of the emergency (e.g. relative's death certificate, summons, immigration or marriage appointment); 6. two (2) current passport photos with plain white background; 7. USPS money order for $75 USD. B. Issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (in Algeria): application form provided by the MFA, completed and signed; proof of foreign residence; consular registration card; statement from any police station in Algeria confirming loss, theft or deterioration; two current passport photos; receipt from Algerian tax services showing payment of 6,000 DA.

106.title: Emergency Passport - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
106.text: registration card; statement from any police station in Algeria confirming loss, theft or deterioration; two current passport photos; receipt from Algerian tax services showing payment of 6,000 DA. Contact: (917) 251-9795.

107.title: Travel Document (Laissez-passer) - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
107.text: Laissez-passer - Consulate General of Algeria in New York. 'The laissez-passer is a travel document issued to Algerian nationals not registered at the Consulate General' to return to Algeria when the passport is lost, stolen or expired; also issued to newborns in the USA whose Algerian parents are visiting as tourists or lack legal immigration status. Valid up to 30 days, one-way to Algeria by the shortest route. 'The laissez-passer request must be submitted to our services at the latest, 72 hours before the departure date.' All applicants: application form filled out and signed; two recent photographs; flight ticket; self-addressed return envelope if mailed back. Adults: proof of Algerian nationality (passport, national identity card, or military card with photo); the damaged Algerian passport, if applicable; signed statement from a Police Department on damage, loss or theft. Newborns/minors: proof of father's or mother's Algerian nationality; original full-version birth certificate of the child; if the father is Algerian and not present, his authorization (notarized if mailed, or legalized by an administrative officer (Commune) in Algeria if he is there).

108.title: Travel Document (Laissez-passer) - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
108.text: birth certificate of the child; if the father is Algerian and not present, his authorization (notarized if mailed, or legalized by an administrative officer (Commune) in Algeria if he is there). Civil status documents (birth/marriage certificates, family book), driving licenses and foreign documents are not accepted as proof of nationality. No fee stated on this page.

109.title: Biometric National Identity Card - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
109.text: Biometric National Identity Card (CNIBE) - Consulate General of Algeria in New York. Issued to Algerian citizens permanently residing abroad after consular registration. Applicants of any age may apply online after obtaining a biometric passport (holders with a National Identification Number (NIN) can use passeport.interieur.gov.dz). Children under 12 are exempt from fingerprinting; their presence is not required for filing or collection. Applicants 12 and older must attend fingerprinting in person; no appointment needed, but sending the application before attending is recommended. First-time (19+): ID form completed and signed; two recent 2x2 inch (51x51 mm) photos, white background, neutral expression, no smile, clear forehead; original 12-S birth certificate; USPS Priority Mail return envelope. Under 19: same, form signed by the legal tutor. Renewal: ID renewal form completed and signed (by legal tutor for minors); two photos; original 12-S birth certificate; USPS Priority Mail return envelope. Option 1: online application; option 2 (if online does not work): submit the renewal documents.

110.title: Biometric National Identity Card - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
110.text: tutor for minors); two photos; original 12-S birth certificate; USPS Priority Mail return envelope. Option 1: online application; option 2 (if online does not work): submit the renewal documents. Fees (official fee page): old ID in possession - free; old ID damaged or lost - $15.00 penalty, USPS money order. No processing time stated.

111.title: Consular Registration - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
111.text: Consular Registration - Consulate General of Algeria in New York. Algerian citizens living permanently overseas must complete consular registration before obtaining passports or registering to vote. A consular card is issued free of charge, valid for 5 years. Submit in person without appointment or by mail to 15 East 47th Street, New York, NY 10017. Cannot apply if you: 1. entered the US temporarily for business (B1), tourism (B2), or both (B1/B2); 2. hold a work permit not valid for re-entry; 3. are considered an undocumented immigrant. Under 19: only the parent's (or legal guardian's) registration is needed; no consular card until age 19. Request types: first-time; renewal; transfer from another embassy/consulate (registration granted once the file is received from the previous post). All requests: application form (Registration_form.pdf) completed and signed; two recent 2x2 inch (51x51 mm) photos; self-addressed stamped envelope.

112.title: Consular Registration - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
112.text: the file is received from the previous post). All requests: application form (Registration_form.pdf) completed and signed; two recent 2x2 inch (51x51 mm) photos; self-addressed stamped envelope. First-time (varies by status - US-born citizen, naturalized, permanent resident, visa holder A/F/G/H/J): original full-size birth certificate (E.C 12 Copie integrale if born in Algeria; any birth certificate if born abroad; US birth certificate for US-born); one parent's birth certificate or Algerian nationality certificate (not needed if parent holds a consular card); if born overseas, certificate of Algerian nationality or birth certificates of two male ascendants born in Algeria; copy of front and back of green card (permanent residents; initial green card for naturalized); copy of US passport or naturalization certificate (citizens); copy of nonimmigrant visa and/or USCIS document (visa holders); copy of US entry visa; copy of Algerian passport photo page if available; proof of employment, self-employment or school enrollment.

113.title: Consular Registration - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
113.text: copy of nonimmigrant visa and/or USCIS document (visa holders); copy of US entry visa; copy of Algerian passport photo page if available; proof of employment, self-employment or school enrollment. Renewal: expired consular card (if available); copy of US passport / naturalization certificate / green card / visa document (if different from initial registration); proof of employment or enrollment (if different); photos; stamped envelope. Transfer of file: same as first-time minus the parent documents.

114.title: Civil Status - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
114.text: Civil Status Services - Consulate General of Algeria in New York. No appointment needed; file in person or by mail. Mailed applications must include a USPS Priority Mail return envelope; incomplete mailed applications are returned. Birth: Algerian parent(s) must report a newborn's birth. The 12-S (extract of birth certificate) is required for a biometric passport or ID card. Born in Algeria: obtain the 12-S online through the Ministry of the Interior website, or at the Town Hall of the birth place in person or through a power of attorney issued by the consulate. Born in the US: Birth Report form completed and signed; original or certified copy of the full birth certificate from city hall including time of birth (returned after verification); copy of proof of Algerian nationality and identity (passport, national ID, consular card, or military card; for minors a parent's); family book if available. Born in another country: same, with the birth certificate from that country. Parents' names must match the Algerian civil status register.

115.title: Civil Status - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
115.text: card; for minors a parent's); family book if available. Born in another country: same, with the birth certificate from that country. Parents' names must match the Algerian civil status register. Marriage: a marriage of an Algerian national in the US must be registered; a family book (livret de famille) is issued after registration, free of charge. Documents: Marriage Registration descriptive form completed and signed; original US marriage certificate (returned after verification); copy of proof of Algerian nationality; original birth certificates of both spouses (the Algerian national's issued within the last three months). Divorce: a US or other foreign divorce has no effect in Algeria unless recognized by an Algerian court ('Exequatur'), carried out in Algeria, optionally through a lawyer. Death / repatriation of remains: the consulate assists families; funeral services handle transfer paperwork; the consulate transcribes the death, issues an Algerian death certificate and the 'Autorisation de Transfert de corps'. Repatriation documents: 1. death report completed and signed; 2. birth certificate of the deceased; 3.

116.title: Civil Status - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
116.text: the death, issues an Algerian death certificate and the 'Autorisation de Transfert de corps'. Repatriation documents: 1. death report completed and signed; 2. birth certificate of the deceased; 3. medical letter from the Department of Health stating the death was not from an infectious or communicable disease; 4. original US death certificate; 5. embalming certificate; 6. transit permit from City Hall; 7. certificate that the body was prepared according to Muslim rituals; 8. copy of the deceased's proof of Algerian nationality; 9. airway bill; 10. family book if available. Death registration only: items 1, 2, 4, 8, 10. Names must match the civil status register. Correction of errors (birth, marriage, death certificates): application form; original certificate from the place of the event (foreign-language documents translated into Arabic); copy of the certificate with the error; supporting identity documents (birth errors), spouses' birth certificates with annotations (marriage errors), or the deceased's birth and marriage certificates and the applicant's birth certificate and proof of relationship (death errors). Submission does not rule out a judicial investigation.

117.title: Civil Status - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
117.text: errors), or the deceased's birth and marriage certificates and the applicant's birth certificate and proof of relationship (death errors). Submission does not rule out a judicial investigation. Fees (official fee page): 12-S birth certificate free; duplicate of family book $25.00; translation of family record book $25.00.

118.title: Criminal Record - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
118.text: Criminal Record (Casier Judiciaire No. 3) - Consulate General of Algeria in New York. Registered members of the Algerian community in the consulate's jurisdiction can request a copy of their criminal record (Bulletin No. 3) through the consulate; requests can also be made directly to the relevant services under a ministerial instruction of June 24, 2010 by the Ministers of Foreign Affairs and Justice. Algerian citizens abroad: application form (PDF); birth certificate; copy of consular card; pre-paid self-addressed return envelope. Non-Algerians who resided in Algeria: application form; valid ID; proof of residency in Algeria; pre-paid self-addressed return envelope. Fee: free (per the official fee page). No appointment needed. Note: the page text refers to '44 states' of jurisdiction, which predates the San Francisco consulate; current NY jurisdiction is 25 states.

119.title: Nationality Certificate - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
119.text: Algerian Nationality Certificate - Consulate General of Algeria in New York. Issued to Algerian nationals established within the consular jurisdiction, under Articles 6 and 7 of the Nationality Law (Order No. 70-86 of 15 December 1970, amended by Order No. 05-01 of 27 February 2005). The Consulate submits the application through the Ministry of Justice platform; after processing by the competent judicial authorities the certificate is delivered electronically, signed. No appointment needed; apply in person or by mail (mail: notarized copies and a USPS Priority Mail return envelope). Identity proof (one): state ID, driver license, US passport or passport card, US military card, military dependent ID, Permanent Resident Card, Certificate of Citizenship, Certificate of Naturalization, Employment Authorization Document, or foreign passport. Documents by case (plus the signed application form): Algerian father, original nationality - applicant's, father's and grandfather's birth certificates. Father acquired nationality - applicant's birth certificate and copy of father's acquisition decree.

120.title: Nationality Certificate - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
120.text: father, original nationality - applicant's, father's and grandfather's birth certificates. Father acquired nationality - applicant's birth certificate and copy of father's acquisition decree. Father's nationality proven by the judiciary - applicant's and father's birth certificates and executive copy of the final judicial decision. Algerian mother, original - applicant's birth certificate plus mother's nationality certificate, or mother's, her father's and her grandfather's birth certificates. Mother acquired - applicant's birth certificate and mother's acquisition decree. Mother proven by judiciary - applicant's and mother's birth certificates and the judicial decision. Unknown parents - full copy of Algerian birth certificate from the place of birth. Named mother only - same plus a certificate from the Directorate of Assisted Childhood. Judicial decision - applicant's birth certificate and executive copy of the decision. All civil status documents must be in the national language and information must be consistent; the judicial authority may require corrections. Fee: free (per the official fee page).

121.title: Power of Attorney - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
121.text: Power of Attorney (Procuration) - Consulate General of Algeria in New York. A legal document that appoints someone (procurator) to manage your personal or business affairs; you can define and limit their authority. Offered only to Algerian citizens, without prior appointment, for use in Algeria. Mail to 15 East 47th Street, New York, NY 10017. Accepted identity documents: passport, national ID card, consular card, military card. Not accepted as proof of nationality: birth certificate, foreign ID documents, Algerian driver license. In person: proxy form signed before a consular officer; original Algerian identity document; USPS money order of $6.25 ('Six Dollars and Twenty-Five Cents') per proxy. By mail: proxy form signed and notarized before a notary public; notarized copy of the Algerian identity document; USPS money order of $6.25 per proxy; optional USPS Priority Mail return envelope.

122.title: Legalization of Documents - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
122.text: Legalization of Documents - Consulate General of Algeria in New York. Commercial documents (for use in Algeria): original document signed by a company official and notarized by an official notary; authentication from the Department of State; translation into French or Arabic by an official translator; 'Seventy-Five Dollars USD ($75) USPS money order per each document'; the object of the contract or business transaction must be stated; certified return envelope if mailed. Other documents: original and a copy of the document to be legalized; 'Two Dollars and Fifty Cents USD ($2.50) USPS money order'. Hours: Tuesday to Saturday, 9 am to 3 pm; closed Sunday and Monday. No appointment needed.

123.title: National Service - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
123.text: National Service - Consulate General of Algeria in New York. The census covers young Algerians born in the USA or elsewhere aged 17 or older registered with the consulate. 'Failure to enroll may result in the loss of the right of exemption, deferment, or deferral of incorporation.' File in person without appointment or by mail. Census: enrollment form completed electronically and hand-signed by the legal guardian; one original Algerian birth certificate; self-addressed stamped envelope for the census certificate. Those who missed the census period are listed automatically according to the law. Deferment (first-time or renewal): application form completed electronically; two 2x2 inch (51x51 mm) photos; copy of school transcript/enrollment or last diploma (school IDs not accepted); one original Algerian birth certificate ('12S is not acceptable'); prepaid USPS Priority return envelope. Exemption: application form; two photos; one original Algerian birth certificate ('12S is not acceptable'); copy of last diploma or enrollment certificate; prepaid USPS Priority return envelope. Social reasons (e.g.

124.title: National Service - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
124.text: form; two photos; one original Algerian birth certificate ('12S is not acceptable'); copy of last diploma or enrollment certificate; prepaid USPS Priority return envelope. Social reasons (e.g. soutien de famille): also original previous deferment document, letter to the Ministry of National Defense submitted under the authority of the Consulate, copy of parents' family record book, documents on brothers' national service position. Lost exemption card replacement: application form; two photos; copy of the exemption if available; loss report form (notarized if mailed). Error correction: hand-signed letter; two photos; original Algerian birth certificate; original deferment or exemption card if available. Request options: regularization, first-time deferment, deferment renewal, exemption for medical reasons, social reasons, presidential measures; age groups 17-18, 19-24, 25+. No fees stated.

125.title: Visa - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
125.text: Visas to Algeria - Consulate General of Algeria in New York. Processes applications from residents of its 25-state jurisdiction. In person or by mail, no appointment; Tuesday through Friday 9:00 am to 3:00 pm (family visas also Saturday). Mail: 15 East 47th Street, New York, NY 10017. Form completed electronically, dated, hand-signed, one photo pasted. Every applicant including children and infants needs documents and fee. Applications with 'erasures, missing information or folded documents' are rejected. Under 18: birth certificate required. Generally issued within eight or ten days of receipt. Apply no more than sixty (60) days before travel. Submission does not guarantee a visa. Payment by Post Office (USPS) money order only. Include a Priority Mail Express return envelope. Common documents: form; one recent standard photo; original passport and copy of photo page (valid at least 6 months, two blank pages); copy of proof of US legal residency; proof of address within the jurisdiction.

126.title: Visa - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
126.text: form; one recent standard photo; original passport and copy of photo page (valid at least 6 months, two blank pages); copy of proof of US legal residency; proof of address within the jurisdiction. Type-specific: Tourist - hotel/travel agency booking or notarized invitation (host in Algeria via City Hall, or Algerian US resident host registered at CG New York), airline itinerary, proof of income - $160. Diplomatic/Official - diplomatic note, invitation if attending a meeting - $160. Press - employment letter, professional ID, equipment list, program (subject to MFA approval) - $160. Business - employer letter accepting financial responsibility, invitation from Algerian partner; holders may not work - $160. Student - acceptance letter, scholarship letter, proof of income - $160. Temporary Work (90 days or less) - employment contract, temporary work authorization from Algerian employment office, employer letter - $190. Cultural - invitation letter, proof of income (subject to MFA approval) - $190. Medical - medical certificate and letter from Algerian healthcare institution - $160. Work - work permit from Algerian employment office, employer letter - $190.

127.title: Visa - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
127.text: (subject to MFA approval) - $190. Medical - medical certificate and letter from Algerian healthcare institution - $160. Work - work permit from Algerian employment office, employer letter - $190. Transit (max 7 days) - hotel reservation, itinerary, proof of income - $160. Family - copy of spouse's proof of Algerian nationality, marriage certificate - $160 (US passport). Fees above are for US passport holders. A family visa fee table without stated nationality also lists: multiple entries less than 90 days $33; multiple entries more than 90 days $66; other categories one entry (30 days) $110.

128.title: Consular Services Fees - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
128.text: Consular Services Fees - Consulate General of Algeria in New York. Payment: USPS money orders only, exact amount, payable to 'Consulate-General of Algeria', with client's name and address; a separate money order per service with the service named in the memo. Not accepted: cash, personal or company checks, certified checks, bank or personal money orders, card payments. Passport, students and children under 19: Standard (28 pages) $37.50; Large (48 pages) $56.25. Passport, employed or unemployed: Standard (28 pages) $75.00; Large (48 pages) $112.50. National identity card: old ID in possession - Free; old ID damaged or lost - $15.00. Visas to Algeria: varies by visa type and bilateral arrangements. Parental authorization for travel $2.50. Legalization of documents $2.50 per document. Certificate conform $2.50 per document. Certified copy $2.50 per document. Legalisation of commercial documents $75.00 per document. Certificate of origin for goods: increased by 400 DA per 10,000 DA of declared value (50% reduction for students and trainees only). Power of attorney $6.25 per proxy. Sworn statement $2.50 per document. Registration of vessels $312.50.

129.title: Consular Services Fees - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
129.text: by 400 DA per 10,000 DA of declared value (50% reduction for students and trainees only). Power of attorney $6.25 per proxy. Sworn statement $2.50 per document. Registration of vessels $312.50. Certificate of seaworthiness of vessels $375.00. Translation of a family record book $25.00. Duplicate of family book $25.00.
