Nationality Certificate Free. Consular card Free. 12-S Birth certificate Free.

130.title: Contact Us - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
130.text: Contact - Consulate General of Algeria in New York. Address: 15 East 47th Street, New York, NY 10017. Phone: (212) 486-6930, (212) 486-6931, (212) 486-6932. Fax: (212) 486-6934. Hotline (green number): (917) 251-9795. Contact form on the site. 'All consular services are available without an appointment, EXCEPT FOR PASSPORTS.'

131.title: States of Jurisdiction - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
131.text: States of Jurisdiction - Consulate General of Algeria in New York (25 states): Alabama, Arkansas, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Vermont, Wisconsin. Consulate General in San Francisco (19 states): California, Arizona, Nevada, Oregon, Washington, Utah, Colorado, Hawaii, Alaska, North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, Oklahoma, Texas, Kansas, Wyoming, Montana, Idaho, New Mexico. Embassy in Washington, D.C.: North Carolina, South Carolina, Delaware, Maryland, Virginia, West Virginia.

132.title: Opening Hours and Holidays - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
132.text: Opening hours - Consulate General of Algeria in New York. General consular services: Tuesday to Saturday, 9:00 am to 3:00 pm. Visa collection: Tuesday to Friday, 9:00 am to 3:00 pm. All consular services are available without an appointment, except passports. Closed: Sunday and Monday (weekly); New Year's Day (January 1); Yennayer Day (January 12); Eid al-Fitr (three days); International Labor Day (May 1); Juneteenth Day (June 19); Eid al-Adha (three days); U.S. Independence Day (July 4); DZ Independence Day (July 5); Islamic New Year (one day); Mawlid al-Nabi Echarif (one day); Algeria Revolution Day (November 1); Veterans' Day (November 11); Thanksgiving Day (last Thursday in November); Christmas Day (December 25).

133.title: Appointments (RDV) - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
133.text: Appointments - Consulate General of Algeria in New York. 'All consular services are available without an appointment, EXCEPT FOR PASSPORTS.' The appointment page is an online booking form; if you do not receive the confirmation email within an hour, check your spam folder. Public hours: Tuesday to Saturday, 9 am to 3 pm; closed Sunday and Monday. Green number: (917) 251-9795.

134.title: File Transfer - Consulate General of Algeria in Brussels
134.text: FILE TRANSFER. Consulate General of Algeria in Brussels. "Consular file transfer is required in event of a change of a residency out of the consular jurisdiction." The request is made to the consulate covering the new area of residence. Algerian citizens who have newly settled in the consular jurisdiction of the Consulate General in Brussels are invited to submit their file transfer request to this office. Documents to submit: 1. Application form duly completed, dated and signed (downloadable from the page). 2. The consular card issued by the consulate holding the file, or a copy of the passport. 3. The residence permit, or the Belgian or Luxembourgish national identity card for dual citizens. 4. A recent proof of address. For any questions or special requests, contact immatriculation@consulatalgerie.be. Any changes in personal situation (profession, marriage, divorce, civil status) must also be notified to the Consulate. The page does not state fees, payment methods or processing times.

135.title: File Transfer - Consulate General of Algeria in Milan
135.text: FILE TRANSFER. Consulate General of Algeria in Milan. "Consular file transfer is required in event of a change of a residency out of the consular jurisdiction." The request is addressed to the consulate covering the new place of residence. Algerian citizens newly settled in the consular jurisdiction of Milan are invited to submit the following documents to the office: - "Application form duly completed, dated and signed to download"; - The consular card issued by the consulate holding the file, or a copy of the passport; - A residence permit, or a national identity card of the host country for dual citizens (the page text says French national identity card); - A recent proof of address. Notification of changes: "any changes in personal situation (profession, marriage, divorce, civil status) have to be notified to the Consulate." The page does not give fees, payment methods, step-by-step procedures or processing times; contact the consulate for these.

136.title: File Transfer - Consulate General of Algeria in London
136.text: FILE TRANSFER. Consulate General of Algeria in London. Algerian nationals already registered at an Algerian embassy or consulate abroad who now live permanently in the UK should "ask for the transfer of their Registration file." The Consulate handles the transfer, and the new registration at the London Consulate is granted once the file has arrived. "In some cases, the agreement of competent authorities in Algeria is needed." Required documents: 1. File transfer application form. 2. First registration application form. 3. (item missing in source numbering) 4. Original current consular registration card. 5. Original proof of legal, permanent residence in the UK. 6. Four recent passport-size photographs. 7. Any additional documents relating to your personal or professional background, if requested. The page does not state fees, payment, or processing times.

137.title: Consulate services - Consulate General of Algeria in London
137.text: Consulate services. Consulate General of Algeria in London. Main duties: the consulate is responsible to "identify, protect the interests, and provide assistance to all Algerian nationals" in its jurisdiction in the UK, in line with local law and policy, and acts as the link between them and Algeria. Services for the Algerian community: registers Algerians living in or visiting its jurisdiction; acts as civil registrar for births, marriages and deaths, and handles documents for the transfer of remains to Algeria; provides notarial services such as powers of attorney, kafala and successions; issues national identity cards, passports and emergency travel documents - only registered citizens qualify for all services except travel documents; handles military (national) service matters: registration (census), deferment and exemptions; provides consular protection in cases of arrest, imprisonment, serious accident or illness, and may assist with repatriation; informs on overseas voting rights, organizes elections and handles proxy voting; oversees economic, commercial, cultural and scientific relations with local authorities and institutions.

138.title: Consulate services - Consulate General of Algeria in London
138.text: informs on overseas voting rights, organizes elections and handles proxy voting; oversees economic, commercial, cultural and scientific relations with local authorities and institutions. Services for the foreign community: the consulate issues entry visas to Algeria for British citizens; other foreign nationals must provide proof of residence in the UK.

139.title: Is your passport ready? (online service) - Consulate General of Algeria in London
139.text: IS YOUR PASSPORT READY? Online service of the Consulate General of Algeria in London. Biometric passports are issued (handed over) Tuesday through Saturday, 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. Applicants can check whether their biometric passport is ready by entering the application registration number shown on their deposit receipt (the page shows an image indicating where the number appears on the receipt). The online passport status check is available at services.mfa.gov.dz/fr/emblondon/passport. The page lists no fees or additional requirements.

140.title: Opening hours - Consulate General of Algeria in London
140.text: Opening hours. Consulate General of Algeria in London. The Consulate is "closed Sundays, Mondays and Algerian holidays." Passport service, civil status office (Etat civil) and other services: Tuesday to Saturday, 9:00 am to 3:00 pm. Visa section: Tuesday to Saturday; application lodging and collection from 9:30 am to 1:00 pm. Public holidays: New Year's Day (1 January); Amazigh New Year (12 January); Good Friday (date changes each year); Labour Day (1 May); Independence Day (5 July); Anniversary of the Revolution (1 November); Christmas Day (25 December); Boxing Day (26 December). Religious holidays: Eid al-Fitr (two days); Eid al-Adha (two days); Awal Muharram; Achoura; Mawlid al-Nabawi al-Sharif. Religious holiday dates follow the lunar calendar.

141.title: Contact - Consulate General of Algeria in London
141.text: Contact. Consulate General of Algeria in London (Ministry of Foreign Affairs and National Community Abroad). Phone: +44 (0)208 752 1177. Fax: +44 (0)208 752 8061. Toll-free (green number): 02087528066. Separate email addresses are listed for general information, visas, civil status, immigration, national service and consular matters. Opening hours: Tuesday to Saturday, 09:00 to 15:00. Visa applications accepted Tuesday to Friday, 09:30 to 13:00. The contact page does not list the physical address or define the consular jurisdiction.

142.title: Emergency Passport - Consulate General of Algeria in London
142.text: Emergency Passport. Consulate General of Algeria in London. Legal basis: Executive Decree n° 16-58 of 3 February 2016 sets the conditions for issuing an Emergency Passport. The Emergency Passport is "exceptionally issued and delivered to the profit of Algerian citizens" whose immigration status regularization has been accepted by the receiving country and who need a valid passport. Application file: an Emergency Passport Application Form and a Description Form. "Note: The validity period of an Emergency Passport is one year running from its issuing date" and it cannot be extended or renewed. The page does not list fees, payment, steps or processing times.

143.title: Power of Attorney - Consulate General of Algeria in London
143.text: POWER OF ATTORNEY. Consulate General of Algeria in London. The power of attorney allows an Algerian citizen living in the UK to appoint someone to carry out an administrative or judicial procedure in Algeria on his/her behalf, for example buying or selling property or running a business. It cannot be used for marriage. The power of attorney is personal: the applicant must attend the Consulate in person. "Applications made by post are no longer accepted." Steps: 1. Complete the application form at the consulate. 2. Sign the form at the consulate in front of consular staff. Documents required - proof of identity, one of: consular registration card; passport; national identity card. "Other documents are not considered valid." Fee: £5. The applicant must be physically present for the Consulate to certify the document.

144.title: Transcription of Civil Records - Consulate General of Algeria in London
144.text: TRANSCRIPTION OF CIVIL RECORDS. Consulate General of Algeria in London. Scope: the London consulate registers births only for children born in the UK or Ireland; for births elsewhere, registration must be made at the Algerian embassy or consulate in the country of birth. Register an Algerian child's birth as soon as you receive the British or Irish birth certificate; do not delay. Application rules: incomplete applications are not accepted; incomplete postal applications may be ignored or returned. Postal applications must include a copy of your signed, valid consular registration card and a prepaid special or recorded delivery envelope for return of documents. Applicants in Ireland must include an £8 postal order for return postage, payable to the Algerian Consulate with your name written on the back; cheques are not accepted and cash must not be sent by post. Unregistered citizens must prove Algerian nationality and identity with an Algerian passport, a CNIA national identity card, or a military card with photo, and must complete the non-registered applicant form and provide two recent passport-size photos with their name on the back.

145.title: Transcription of Civil Records - Consulate General of Algeria in London
145.text: passport, a CNIA national identity card, or a military card with photo, and must complete the non-registered applicant form and provide two recent passport-size photos with their name on the back. In-person applications are accepted Tuesday to Saturday, mornings only, 9 am to 12 noon. Births registered in the same year as the child's birth get priority. Required documents (births in the UK or Ireland): 1. Application form completed in Arabic, dated and signed. 2. Original and copy of the full British or Irish birth certificate (short certificates are not accepted). 3. Family book (livret de famille), if you have one. 4. Copy of the applicant's consular registration card (registered citizens). 5. For unregistered citizens: proof of Algerian nationality and identity, the non-registered application form, and two passport-size photos. Processing time: depends on the number of applications and may take more than a month. Before applying for a child's passport, make sure the child is already registered; otherwise, provide the Algerian family book or the birth certificate issued by the Algerian embassy or consulate where the birth was registered.

146.title: Passport Renewal - Consulate General of Algeria in Milan
146.text: Passport Renewal. Consulate General of Algeria in Milan. Required documents (original and copy): - Valid consular registration card. - Passport application form, completed, dated and signed (available at the consulate or downloadable). - Photocopy of the first page of the expired passport. - Residence permit, or Italian identity card for dual nationals. - Proof of residence within the consular district. - Proof of activity. - Two identical identity photos. - Payment of the chancery fee. - Original 12S birth certificate plus a copy, for applicants renewing a passport issued by another consulate or in Algeria. Fees: adults €60; minor children, or students presenting a valid university education certificate, €30. When a passport can be renewed: "Less than six (06) months before expiration"; when the pages are nearly full of stamps (maximum of three pages left); in case of loss, theft or damage. The page does not state processing times or payment method.

147.title: Power of Attorney - Consulate General of Algeria in Milan
147.text: POWER OF ATTORNEY. Consulate General of Algeria in Milan. To have a power of attorney (procuration) issued, "the applicant must be present with a valid Algerian passport or identity card". Only a valid Algerian passport or national identity card is accepted as proof of identity. A downloadable application form is provided on the page. The page does not state fees, payment methods, steps or processing times; contact the consulate for these details.

148.title: Power of Attorney (Procuration) for the Algerian Citizen Only - Embassy of Algeria in Washington
148.text: Power of Attorney (Procuration) for Algerian Citizens Only. Embassy of Algeria in Washington, D.C. The Embassy issues this document so that Algerian citizens residing in its consular district can authorize a person living in Algeria to act and transact on their behalf. The applicant must "necessarily introduce his/her proxy in person". Walk-in requirements: - Completed application form, signed in front of a consular officer. - Original proof of identity: consular card, passport or national ID; no other documents are accepted. - USPS money order of $6.25 per proxy. Mail-in requirements: - Completed application form signed by the applicant and legalized by a public notary, with the notary's seal on the form. - Notarized copy of a valid Algerian ID (consular card, passport or national ID). - USPS money order of $6.25 per proxy. - Prepaid return envelope. Fee: $6.25 per proxy, payable by USPS money order only, made payable to the Embassy of Algeria. Processing time is not stated.

149.title: Consular pass declaration - Embassy of Algeria in Riyadh
149.text: Consular pass declaration (laissez-passer). Embassy of Algeria in Riyadh. The consular pass is issued to "non-resident Algerian citizens, who came on a visit visa" to Saudi Arabia and have lost their passport or whose passport has expired, allowing them to return to Algeria by the most direct route available. Required documents: - Proof of identity (passport or national identification card). - Copy of the entry visa to Saudi Arabia. - Passport loss certificate from the local authorities. - Three photos. - Confirmed travel ticket. The file is submitted to the consular office. Timing: submit the file "not less than a week and not more than 10 days" before departure. The transit document is issued only three days before departure. The page does not list fees or payment methods.

150.title: Consulate services - Consulate General of Algeria in Jeddah
150.text: Consulate services. Consulate General of Algeria in Jeddah. Passport, registration and change of residence: registers and re-registers nationals residing in the consular district and issues consular registration cards; accepts transfers of resident files from other consular posts; receives passport applications and renewals and performs biometric enrollment; delivers passports and national identity cards once produced in Algeria; issues change-of-residence certificates. Civil status: transcribes civil status documents; issues full copies for nationals born in the district; issues special 12S certificates for nationals transcribed in the Jeddah birth registers; issues certified extracts of civil status documents drawn up in Algeria or abroad upon presentation of the family record book. Legalization and certification: certifies powers of attorney and signatures of Algerian nationals; legalizes Algerian-issued deeds and documents and certifies copies; legalizes commercial documents; legalizes deeds issued by the host state and certifies copies. National service: receives national service files and delivers related documents.

151.title: Consulate services - Consulate General of Algeria in Jeddah
151.text: and certifies copies; legalizes commercial documents; legalizes deeds issued by the host state and certifies copies. National service: receives national service files and delivers related documents. Social and legal: receives requests for criminal record extract no. 03 and issues it; receives driving licence capacity certificate applications, issued after preparation by the Algerian authority; handles the protection of Algerian nationals' interests under international conventions. Visa: processes visa applications. Hajj and Umrah: manages Hajj and Umrah files. Hours and contacts are not listed on this page.

152.title: Extracts of Civil Registration - Consulate General of Algeria in Istanbul
152.text: Extracts of Civil Registration. Consulate General of Algeria in Istanbul. The Consulate General notifies Algerian municipalities of civil status changes such as marriage and death. Changes made under judicial decisions of the host country are not recognized until the court of Sidi M'hamed (Algiers Judicial Council) issues an executive formula (exequatur) for them. Death certificate: the original authenticated death certificate; an identity document plus the deceased's birth certificate. Marriage certificate - to register (transcribe) a marriage contract with the Istanbul Consulate General, provide: the original marriage certificate; birth certificates of the husband and the wife; an Algerian nationality certificate for either spouse; a completed form; identity photos of both spouses. Birth certificate: the person concerned must hold Algerian nationality; the original certified birth certificate of the newborn; a clearly completed form; the family book (livret de famille) so the newborn can be added. The page does not specify fees, payment methods or processing times.

153.title: Emergency Passport - Consulate General of Algeria in Milan
153.text: Emergency Passport. Consulate General of Algeria in Milan. The emergency passport is a non-biometric, machine-readable travel document issued abroad by Algerian embassies and consulates, and in some cases by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Algiers. It is valid for 3 months to 1 year depending on the purpose, and cannot be extended. It is issued in emergencies and only exceptionally to: - Algerians living abroad, registered at a consular post, who have no passport and must travel urgently for family, professional, administrative or health reasons; - Algerians temporarily in a country other than their country of residence whose passport was lost, damaged, stolen or expired; - Algerians living abroad who are not registered at a consular post, whose residency file has been accepted by the host country, and who need a valid passport. Required documents: - A written request explaining the purpose of the application; - A document supporting the request; - The completed application form, signed by the applicant or, for minors, by the legal guardian; - Proof of Algerian nationality (e.g.

154.title: Emergency Passport - Consulate General of Algeria in Milan
154.text: of the application; - A document supporting the request; - The completed application form, signed by the applicant or, for minors, by the legal guardian; - Proof of Algerian nationality (e.g. passport copy, birth certificate, or form S12); - A copy of the consular registration card, for registered citizens; - Two recent, identical, unframed digital photos with a white background. Fees: 60 € stamp duty. If the passport was lost, stolen or destroyed: a police statement (declaration) from the local authorities and a 100 € loss fee. Steps: 1. Submit the application to the Consulate General at least one week in advance. 2. After review and acceptance, an appointment is scheduled. 3. At the appointment, bring the original documents that were sent by email. 4. The emergency passport must be returned when the biometric passport is issued and collected. Applications can be sent by email to biometrie@consulatgeneralalgeriemilan.it.

155.title: Opening hours - Consulate General of Algeria in Milan
155.text: Opening hours. Consulate General of Algeria in Milan. Consular services are available without an appointment. The office is open to the public Tuesday through Saturday, 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM. Visa services: application submission Tuesday to Friday, 9:00 AM to 11:00 AM; collection Tuesday to Friday, 2:00 PM to 3:00 PM. Applicants should check the section for their application type on the website to make sure their file is complete.

156.title: Opening hours - Consulate General of Algeria in Istanbul
156.text: Opening hours. Consulate General of Algeria in Istanbul. "Consular Services are delivered without appointments." Services run Monday to Friday, 9:00 am to 3:00 pm. Department phone numbers: Social Affairs and Document Authentication Department: +90 501 813 22 80. Civil Status Department: +90 501 813 22 78. Consular Registration and Biometric Documents Department: +90 501 813 22 79. Visa, Commercial, and Maritime Document Authentication Department: +90 501 086 11 80. On-Call and General Affairs Department: +90 501 813 22 77.

157.title: Transfer of remains of deceased citizens - Consulate General of Algeria in London
157.text: Transfer of remains of deceased citizens - Death & transfer of corpse. Consulate General of Algeria in London. The Consulate assists families of Algerian nationals who die abroad with preparing the remains and arranging their transfer to Algeria, in line with the family's wishes and local and Algerian regulations. "The Consulate does not pay the transfer of the remains." The Consulate should be contacted immediately after the death of an Algerian national so it can inform the family and give assistance and advice. A funeral service (undertaker) appointed by the family handles all administrative formalities; on request, the Consulate can recommend reliable undertakers. The Consulate informs the family and the relevant Algerian authorities of the death and the arrival date, and issues the death certificate and the "Authorisation de Transfert de corps". Documents required for the transfer authorisation: 1. Birth certificate (if the citizen is not registered at the Consulate). 2. Medical certificate "Free from infection" issued by the hospital or the doctor who certified the death. 3. Death certificate. 4. "Out of England" certificate issued by the Coroner. 5.

158.title: Transfer of remains of deceased citizens - Consulate General of Algeria in London
158.text: Consulate). 2. Medical certificate "Free from infection" issued by the hospital or the doctor who certified the death. 3. Death certificate. 4. "Out of England" certificate issued by the Coroner. 5. Embalming certificate issued by the funeral services. 6. Undertaker's certificate confirming the coffin contains only the remains of the named deceased. 7. Certificate confirming the body was laid out according to Muslim rituals. 8. The deceased's identity documents, including the consular registration card. No fees or processing times are stated.

159.title: Consular Pass (Laissez-Passer) - Consulate General of Algeria in London
159.text: CONSULAR PASS - Travel document (Laissez-Passer). Consulate General of Algeria in London. "The Laissez-passer is a travel document issued in exceptional cases to enable the beneficiary to go back to Algeria." It cannot be used as an identity document, has very limited validity, and should only be used to enter Algeria on a direct flight. It is issued to Algerian citizens not registered at the Consulate who have reported their passport lost or stolen and wish to return to Algeria as soon as possible. Required documents: 1. Application form, completed and signed. 2. Declaration of passport loss. 3. Proof of Algerian nationality: original Algerian passport, national identity card, or military card with photograph (driving licences and birth certificates are not accepted). 4. Four recent photographs. 5. Travel ticket. Important notes: 1. If you cannot provide any of the documents above, you need a certified copy of one of them plus a declaration from two Algerian nationals registered at the Consulate confirming your nationality (downloadable form). 2. Applications for a voluntary return should be made "at least five (5) working days before the date of travel." Fees are not stated.

160.title: Exemption procedure (National Service) - Consulate General of Algeria in London
160.text: Exemption procedure - National Service. Consulate General of Algeria in London. Exemption from national service may be granted for the following reasons. 1. Ordinary application (applicants who have completed or abandoned their studies). Documents: completed, signed application form; original birth certificate, not an S12 extract (those born in the UK obtain it from the Consulate; those born in Algeria from the baladiya of birth); copy of the consular registration card; proof of UK residence (British passport, biometric residence permit, utility bill or bank statement); two passport-sized photographs; copy of an Algerian or British diploma, or, if studies were abandoned, the last school enrolment certificate; copy of a work contract or proof of paid work (e.g. payslips for the last three months). 2. Medical reasons: in addition to the above, evidence of the illness or physical or mental disability (medical certificates, X-rays if available, medical report). Documents in English must be translated into Arabic or French. 3.

161.title: Exemption procedure (National Service) - Consulate General of Algeria in London
161.text: to the above, evidence of the illness or physical or mental disability (medical certificates, X-rays if available, medical report). Documents in English must be translated into Arabic or French. 3. Social reasons (supporting the family, or other socially justified reason): in addition to the documents above, an application addressed to the Ministry of National Defence submitted through the Consulate; copy of the parents' family record book; father's death certificate, or parents' divorce certificate, or father's certificate of unemployment, retirement or disability, where applicable; copy of work contract or proof of paid work; documents showing the brothers' status regarding national service. 4. Algerian-French dual nationals: under the Algerian-French Agreement on National Service of 11 October 1983, exemption may be granted with the deferment or exemption documents above plus the "Déclaration d'Option" and "Certificat des Services" issued by the French military authorities. 5.

162.title: Exemption procedure (National Service) - Consulate General of Algeria in London
162.text: 11 October 1983, exemption may be granted with the deferment or exemption documents above plus the "Déclaration d'Option" and "Certificat des Services" issued by the French military authorities. 5. Presidential measures: completed, signed application form; original birth certificate (not S12); current-year school enrolment certificate or work certificate; copy of consular registration card; four passport-sized photographs; proof of UK residence. Fees and processing times are not stated.

163.title: Census/Regularization (National Service) - Consulate General of Algeria in London
163.text: Census/Regularization - National Service. Consulate General of Algeria in London. Census: national service census is mandatory for Algerians who turn 17, live within the consulate's jurisdiction and are registered with it. "Failure to enrol shall involve the loss of the right of exemption, deferment, and deferral of incorporation." 1. Deferment (Sursis): open to citizens aged 19 or older; covers the full period of study and is renewed yearly until studies end or stop. First application: signed application form; original birth certificate, not an S12 extract (from the Consulate if born in the UK, from the Baladiya if born in Algeria); current-year school enrolment certificate; copy of consular registration card; four passport-sized photos; copy of proof of UK residence (residence card, British passport, biometric residence permit, utility bill or bank statement). Extension: signed application form; copy of consular registration card; original previous deferment certificate; current-year school enrolment certificate. Submit applications or extensions at the beginning of each academic year to avoid delays. 2.

164.title: Census/Regularization (National Service) - Consulate General of Algeria in London
164.text: registration card; original previous deferment certificate; current-year school enrolment certificate. Submit applications or extensions at the beginning of each academic year to avoid delays. 2. Deferral of incorporation (Report d'incorporation): granted if your brother is serving in or has been recalled to the army, or if you have a duly justified temporary impediment; provide the same documents as for deferment plus evidence supporting the reason. Bring photocopies of the required documents to speed up processing.

165.title: Criminal Record - Consulate General of Algeria in Istanbul
165.text: CRIMINAL RECORD. Consulate General of Algeria in Istanbul. "Algerian citizens registered with the services of the Algerian Consulate in Istanbul and born in Algeria" can obtain criminal record certificate (casier judiciaire) No. 03 directly from the Consulate General. Foreign nationals who have lived in Algeria are also eligible. Applications are submitted in person. Required: 1. Completed criminal record certificate request form. 2. Birth certificate, if born in Algeria. 3. Algerian citizens: Algerian identity card. 4. Foreign nationals: identity card and any document proving former residence in Algeria. Fees and processing times are not stated.

166.title: Travel Document (Laissez Passer) - Embassy of Algeria in Washington
166.text: Travel Document (Laissez Passer). Embassy of Algeria in Washington, D.C. The laissez-passer is a "temporary travel document issued to Algerian nationals who are not registered at the Algerian Embassy" to allow them to return to Algeria after their passport was lost, stolen or expired. It is also issued to newborns in the U.S. whose Algerian parents are visiting on a tourist visa or lack legal immigration status. It is valid for 30 days and only for a one-way trip to Algeria by the shortest route. Required documents: completed, signed laissez-passer application form; two recent passport-size photographs; confirmed flight ticket; self-addressed return envelope (only if the document will be mailed). Adults: proof of Algerian nationality - Algerian passport (if available), or Algerian National ID or Military ID card with photo; if the passport is damaged, submit the damaged passport; if lost or stolen, submit a Lost or Stolen Passport Form. Newborns and minors: proof of Algerian nationality of at least one parent (e.g.

167.title: Travel Document (Laissez Passer) - Embassy of Algeria in Washington
167.text: if the passport is damaged, submit the damaged passport; if lost or stolen, submit a Lost or Stolen Passport Form. Newborns and minors: proof of Algerian nationality of at least one parent (e.g. passport); original full-version birth certificate of the child; if the father is not present at the Embassy, an authorization letter from him - notarized if applying by mail, or legalized by a Commune administrative officer if he is in Algeria. Civil status documents and foreign documents are not accepted as proof of nationality. "The laissez-passer request must be submitted at least 72 hours before departure."

168.title: Other Services (legalization, parental authorization, kafala, casier judiciaire, J-1 waiver) - Embassy of Algeria in Washington
168.text: Other services. Embassy of Algeria in Washington, D.C. 1. US-issued documents (legalization): the original document must be notarized, carry the apostille of the issuing state, and be certified by the U.S. Department of State; include a photocopy; fee $75 (non-refundable) USPS money order per document; include a prepaid return envelope. 2. Travel document (laissez-passer): issued in exceptional cases to return to Algeria; not an identity document; valid 30 days only; requirements: application form, declaration of passport loss, proof of Algerian nationality (national ID card or military card with photo; driving licences and birth certificates not accepted), four recent photographs, travel ticket. 3. Minor child travel (parental authorization): an Algerian minor aged 19 or younger travelling without his parents needs a notarized travel authorization signed by the father, which border authorities may require. Not required if the parents are divorced or separated, the minor lives abroad with the mother, and the mother holds a court order granting full custody (to be shown when leaving Algeria).

169.title: Other Services (legalization, parental authorization, kafala, casier judiciaire, J-1 waiver) - Embassy of Algeria in Washington
169.text: require. Not required if the parents are divorced or separated, the minor lives abroad with the mother, and the mother holds a court order granting full custody (to be shown when leaving Algeria). Requirements: application form; original and copy of the minor's full birth certificate or family book; father's consular card, national ID or passport; money order (fee listed as $2.50). Valid three months. The father or guardian must be present; if the father or both parents are deceased, a parent or guardian must be present. A mother travelling with the child must provide her residence card, a copy of the custody document, proof of the child's legal presence abroad and the family booklet. 4. Power of attorney (procuration), Algerian citizens only: in person - form signed before a consular officer, original consular card/passport/national ID, $6.25 USPS money order per proxy; by mail - notarized form with notary seal, notarized copy of valid Algerian ID, $6.25 USPS money order per proxy, prepaid return envelope. 5.

170.title: Other Services (legalization, parental authorization, kafala, casier judiciaire, J-1 waiver) - Embassy of Algeria in Washington
170.text: ID, $6.25 USPS money order per proxy; by mail - notarized form with notary seal, notarized copy of valid Algerian ID, $6.25 USPS money order per proxy, prepaid return envelope. 5. Transfer of property in an estate: property (including vehicles) must have been fully owned by the deceased; assets must be repatriated within one year of the date the "Fredha" was established; applicant must be authorized by the heirs and hold a notarized special power of attorney; documents: dated and signed inventory of the estate legalized by consular services ($7.50 stamp duty), notarized copy of the Fredha deed, death certificate, special power of attorney, customs declaration for release for consumption. 6. Legal adoption (Kafala): age limits 60 for men and 55 for women; single, widowed and divorced women may apply under similar conditions; the Kafil must be in good health, Muslim, of Algerian nationality, with suitable accommodation; documents: written request with reasons, both spouses' birth certificates, family form, medical certificates, criminal records from the country of residence, work certificate, three months of pay stubs, copy of consular card, property title or lease; all documents

171.title: Other Services (legalization, parental authorization, kafala, casier judiciaire, J-1 waiver) - Embassy of Algeria in Washington
171.text: family form, medical certificates, criminal records from the country of residence, work certificate, three months of pay stubs, copy of consular card, property title or lease; all documents translated into Arabic or French. 7. Judicial records (Casier Judiciaire No. 3): for Algerians abroad and foreign nationals who lived in Algeria; requirements: original full birth certificate, valid ID, proof of residence in Algeria (foreign nationals only), self-addressed prepaid envelope, signed application form. 8. Waiver (Attestation de Non-Objection) for J-1 visa holders subject to the two-year home-residence requirement (INA 212(e)): copy of consular registration card; copy of the J-1 waiver recommendation application (all pages); notarized affidavit confirming no obligations to any Algerian public or private entity; job offer on the institution's letterhead. 9. Elections: to be on the electoral roll a citizen must be registered at the embassy, be 18 on Election Day and enjoy civil and political rights; ordinary reviews at the end of each year, exceptional reviews when an election is announced. Contact: (202) 265-2800 or consular-section@algerianembassy.org.

172.title: Biometric Passport - Embassy of Algeria in Washington
172.text: Biometric Passport. Embassy of Algeria in Washington, D.C. Biometric passports are issued only after consular registration is completed. Children under 12 do not need to be fingerprinted in person or collect the passport at the consulate; all documents are sent by mail. Applicants 12 and older must visit for fingerprinting (no appointment needed); mailing the application first can speed up the process. Renewals should be submitted at least six months before the current passport expires. Passports are produced in Algeria and take several weeks; you can track your application one week after fingerprinting with your receipt number. Required documents: completed application form (signed by the legal guardian if applicable); one passport photo meeting size, background and pose requirements; S12 birth certificate, only if your previous biometric passport was not issued by the Embassy in Washington; copy of a valid consular registration card; current or expired passport - if lost or damaged, a Passport Lost or Stolen Form and a penalty fee (lower for students and minors); proof of legal U.S. residency (U.S.

173.title: Biometric Passport - Embassy of Algeria in Washington
173.text: consular registration card; current or expired passport - if lost or damaged, a Passport Lost or Stolen Form and a penalty fee (lower for students and minors); proof of legal U.S. residency (U.S. passport, Green Card or appropriate visa); proof of employment or school enrollment; proof of U.S. address (utility bill or lease); prepaid USPS Priority Mail return envelope with tracking number. Fees: 28-page passport - adults (19+) $75.00, minors and students $37.50; 48-page passport - adults $112.50, minors and students $56.25. Payment: only U.S. Postal Service money orders, payable to "Embassy of Algeria"; no other payment methods accepted.

174.title: Consular Registration (consular card) - Embassy of Algeria in Washington
174.text: Consular Registration. Embassy of Algeria in Washington, D.C. "The Embassy of Algeria urges Algerian citizens residing permanently abroad to complete their consular registration." Registration is required for passport issuance and voter registration. Algerian citizens aged 19 and over can apply and receive a consular card valid for five years. Married Algerian women may, where applicable, be registered under their husband's file. Children under 19 are generally registered under a parent's file. The consular card is free of charge. Applications can be made in person without an appointment, or by mail to the Embassy in Washington, D.C. (The page refers to a personalised checklist of documents.)

175.title: Consular registration and other services - Embassy of Algeria in Abu Dhabi
175.text: Consular registration. Embassy of Algeria in Abu Dhabi. Registration is for citizens who are regular residents; it allows the embassy to locate citizens and provides consular protection, easier access to administrative documents, and a one-time certificate of change of residence for moving belongings and a tourist car upon final return. Documents: original birth certificate; original father's birth certificate; nationality certificate (or the father's and grandfather's birth certificates for those born in Algeria); passport copy; copy of valid UAE (Abu Dhabi) residence permit; five identical recent photos; work certificate, or university certificate for students; family situation: marriage contract (married), copy of divorce judgment (divorced), or husband's death certificate (widowed). The applicant must appear in person. The registration card is free and valid five years. Renewal of the card is required after a change in civil status, profession or residence: expired card, document reflecting the change, two recent photos; attendance required.

176.title: Consular registration and other services - Embassy of Algeria in Abu Dhabi
176.text: and valid five years. Renewal of the card is required after a change in civil status, profession or residence: expired card, document reflecting the change, two recent photos; attendance required. Re-registration: citizens who obtained a certificate of change of residence or requested a deletion certificate must register again under the same conditions as a first registration. Elections: voter cards are issued to citizens on the electoral roll (registered at the embassy, 18 on Election Day, enjoying civil and political rights); ordinary review yearly from 1 to 31 October; exceptional review when an election is announced. Power of attorney (procuration), Algerian citizens only, in person: completed form signed before a consular officer; original consular card, passport or national ID; postal money order payable to the Embassy for each proxy. Judicial records (Casier Judiciaire No. 3): original full birth certificate, valid ID, proof of residence in Algeria (foreign nationals), self-addressed prepaid envelope, signed application form.

177.title: Consular registration and other services - Embassy of Algeria in Abu Dhabi
177.text: Judicial records (Casier Judiciaire No. 3): original full birth certificate, valid ID, proof of residence in Algeria (foreign nationals), self-addressed prepaid envelope, signed application form. Laissez-passer: exceptional, not an identity document, valid 30 days; application form, declaration of passport loss, proof of nationality (national ID or military card with photo; driving licence and birth certificate not accepted), four recent photos, travel ticket. Minor child travel: a minor aged 19 or younger travelling without a parent needs a notarized parental travel authorization signed by the father (not required where the mother holds a court order granting full custody and the child lives abroad with her); documents: form, child's full birth certificate or family book, father's consular card/ID/passport, money order; valid three months; father or guardian must attend. National military service: registration required at age 18; citizens who applied for deferment or exemption cards should contact the Office of Consular Affairs. (Note: some text on this page appears copied from the Washington embassy template.)

178.title: Contact - Embassy of Algeria in Abu Dhabi
178.text: Contact. Embassy of Algeria in Abu Dhabi. Phone: 0097124448949. Fax: 0097124447068. Email: ambalg@embassy-algeria-uae.com (general); cultural@embassy-algeria-uae.com; economic@embassy-algeria-uae.com. Working hours - Consular Department: Sunday to Wednesday, 9:00 a.m. to 2:30 p.m.; Thursday, 9:00 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. Other embassy services: Sunday, 11:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; Monday to Thursday, 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. Address: Zayed the First Street, Electra, behind the Holiday Inn Hotel, Building 05, Abu Dhabi. For emergencies, a toll-free number is indicated.

179.title: Transferring the body of a deceased Algerian citizen abroad - Embassy of Algeria in Riyadh
179.text: Transferring the body of a deceased Algerian citizen abroad. Embassy of Algeria in Riyadh. If an Algerian citizen dies abroad, relatives must submit a file to the consular services to obtain a permit to transport the body. The file must include: a death certificate from the Civil Status Department; a burial permit; an embalming certificate; a transfer authorization; and a certificate of absence of contagious disease. Fees and processing times are not stated.

180.title: Consular registration - Embassy of Algeria in Berlin
180.text: Consular registration. Embassy of Algeria in Berlin. "Consular registration is an administrative procedure concerning Algerian nationals" legally residing abroad; it is required to receive consular protection and services. First registration: appear in person at the consulate covering your place of residence. Minors under 19 are registered at the request of the person holding parental authority; for divorced parents, the divorce judgment must be presented. Documents for first registration: completed, dated and signed application form (Forms section); Algerian passport or national identity card, with photocopy of the first three passport pages and the pages showing German entry visas; Algerian nationality certificate, or alternative birth certificates if unavailable; naturalization decree if Algerian nationality was acquired; residence permit (or renewal receipt) or valid national identity card of the host country, with photocopy; proof of address dated within the last three months, with photocopy; for people staying with a host, a sworn statement from the host legalized by the local town hall plus the host's proof of address; proof of employment with photocopy; four recent passport

181.title: Consular registration - Embassy of Algeria in Berlin
181.text: photocopy; for people staying with a host, a sworn statement from the host legalized by the local town hall plus the host's proof of address; proof of employment with photocopy; four recent passport photos (3.5 x 4.5 cm); marriage certificate or family booklet if married; divorce judgment (original and copy) for divorced women. Spouses and minor children are registered as dependents; a spouse provides the same documents plus a marriage certificate. Minors: birth certificate (full copy if born in Algeria, transcribed extract if born abroad); residence permit or national ID with photocopy; two recent identical photos; the father or legal guardian must be present. Card renewal: the consular card is valid five years; submit the expired card, two recent colour photos from the same series, residence permit and photocopy, and a new registration certificate if the address changed. Moving to another consular district: present your consular card, registration certificate and valid residence permit at the new consulate. Report any change of civil status, address or occupation with supporting documents.

182.title: Consular registration - Embassy of Algeria in Berlin
182.text: district: present your consular card, registration certificate and valid residence permit at the new consulate. Report any change of civil status, address or occupation with supporting documents. Removal from the register: upon death, permanent return to Algeria, change of consular district, handwritten request, or absence exceeding 10 years; removal also removes you from the electoral roll. Fees: consular registration card free of charge; removal certificate subject to a stamp fee.

183.title: Other services (laissez-passer, parental authorization, casier judiciaire, procuration, national service) - Embassy of Algeria in Berlin
183.text: Other services. Embassy of Algeria in Berlin. Travel document (laissez-passer): issued in exceptional cases to return to Algeria; "It cannot be used as an identity document"; valid 30 days only. Required: application form; declaration of passport loss; proof of Algerian nationality (national ID or military card with photo; driving licence and birth certificate not accepted); four recent photographs; travel ticket. Minor child travel (parental authorization): Algerian minors aged 19 or younger travelling without their parents need a notarized travel authorization signed by the father; not required if the parents are divorced or separated, the minor lives abroad with the mother and she holds a court order granting full custody. Required: application form; original and copy of the full birth certificate or family book; father's consular card, national ID or passport; money order. Valid three months; the father or guardian must be present. For the custody exemption, the mother provides her residence card, copy of the custody document, proof of the child's legal residence or schooling abroad, and the family booklet or other proof of family ties.

184.title: Other services (laissez-passer, parental authorization, casier judiciaire, procuration, national service) - Embassy of Algeria in Berlin
184.text: exemption, the mother provides her residence card, copy of the custody document, proof of the child's legal residence or schooling abroad, and the family booklet or other proof of family ties. Judicial records (Casier Judiciaire No 3): for Algerians abroad and foreign nationals who lived in Algeria; original full birth certificate, valid ID, proof of residence in Algeria (foreign nationals), self-addressed prepaid envelope, signed application form. Power of attorney (procuration), Algerian citizens only: applicant appears in person; form signed before the consular officer; original consular card, passport or national ID; postal money order payable to the Embassy for each proxy. Elections: registered citizens receive a voting card (must be registered at the Embassy, 18 on Election Day, with civil and political rights); ordinary review every year from 1 to 31 October; exceptional review when an election is announced. National military service: citizens who applied for deferment or exemption cards should contact Consular Affairs; registration is required at age 18. (Note: parts of this page reproduce the Washington embassy template text.)

185.title: Consular Registration - Consulate General of Algeria in Geneva
185.text: CONSULAR REGISTRATION. Consulate General of Algeria in Geneva (page as published; its jurisdiction line names Bas-Rhin (67), Haut-Rhin (68) and Vosges (88), apparently copied from the Strasbourg consulate template). Consular registration is an administrative procedure for Algerian citizens regularly residing abroad. "The consular registration card is issued free of charge." It is valid five years and renewal must be requested. Changes in civil status, address or profession must be reported with supporting documents. Registered persons who definitively return to Algeria must request removal from the consular registers. First registration (originals plus A4 photocopies): completed, dated and signed application form; Algerian passport with copies of the first three pages, visa page and Schengen entry page; birth certificate (12 S) with copy; father's full birth certificate (if born in Algeria), or father's and grandfather's full birth certificates (if born abroad); naturalization decree if applicable; proof of family status (family record book, marriage certificate or divorce judgment); residence permit with an address in the jurisdiction, renewal receipt, or valid national ID card;

186.title: Consular Registration - Consulate General of Algeria in Geneva
186.text: if applicable; proof of family status (family record book, marriage certificate or divorce judgment); residence permit with an address in the jurisdiction, renewal receipt, or valid national ID card; recent proof of residence (under three months) or accommodation certificate legalized by the city hall; proof of activity (work certificate, payslip, scholarship certificate, unemployment notice, disability or retirement notice); five recent passport photos 3.5 x 4.5 cm. Spouses and minor children are registered as dependents; the spouse submits the same documents. Minors: legal guardian's registration card; child's 12 S birth certificate with copy; DCEM or national ID card for dual citizens; two recent photos; "The presence of the legal guardian is mandatory." Renewal: expired card; completed form; proof of regular stay with copy; proof of residence with copy if the address changed; two recent photos; work certificate, payslips or attendance certificate for students and trainees. Re-registration (after a certificate of change of residence, personal request, or absence of more than 10 years): same documents as the initial registration.

187.title: National Military Service - Embassy of Algeria in Riyadh
187.text: National Military Service. Embassy of Algeria in Riyadh. Requests for registration (census), postponement (deferment) or exemption are submitted to the consular authority, which forwards them to the competent authorities in Algeria; applicants are notified when responses arrive. Registration: "Those concerned should approach the consular authority before December 01, 2027" - this concerns the class of 2027, i.e. Algerian citizens residing abroad born in 2007. Documents: completed registration form; birth certificate; two photos; copy of the legal guardian's consular registration card. Postponement: written request; copy of passport; copy of residence document; copy of consular card; justification (usually a university certificate); copies of previous postponement certificates, if any. Exemption: written request; copy of passport; copy of residence card; copy of consular card; justification depending on the reason (work certificate, medical report, or file of an only son supporting the family); copies of previous postponement certificates, if any; four photos. No fees are listed.

188.title: Consular registration (first registration, renewal, transfer, deletion) - Embassy of Algeria in Washington
188.text: Consular registration. Embassy of Algeria in Washington, D.C. First registration - documents: signed application form; original full birth certificate; original birth or death certificate of the applicant's father; if born abroad, birth certificates of two paternal ancestors born in Algeria, or a certificate of Algerian nationality; marriage certificate if married; record of divorce judgment if divorced; copy of proof of legal presence in the US (long-stay visa, green card or US passport - photocopy of the passport's first page and US visa page); proof of address within the Embassy's consular district; statement of employment or university registration; three recent passport-size photos (frontal, same batch, unedited, white background, no glasses except prescription), with first and last names written in pencil on the back. Notice: the applicant must appear in person with the original proof of legal presence in the US. The registration card is valid five years and must then be renewed (Art. 19, Presidential Decree 02-405 of 2002); failure to renew within ten years results in removal from the register (Art. 20).

189.title: Consular registration (first registration, renewal, transfer, deletion) - Embassy of Algeria in Washington
189.text: The registration card is valid five years and must then be renewed (Art. 19, Presidential Decree 02-405 of 2002); failure to renew within ten years results in removal from the register (Art. 20). Renewal - documents: signed application form; expired registration card (if lost, stolen or damaged, a signed declaration of loss notarized with the notary's seal and a $2.50 penalty paid by US Postal Service money order only, payable to the Embassy of Algeria); two passport-size photos; copy of proof of legal presence in the US; proof of address within the consular district; statement of employment or university registration; self-addressed prepaid envelope. The applicant must sign the registration card when it arrives by mail. Transfer of consular registration - documents: signed application form; original consular registration card; two passport-size photos; copy of proof of legal presence (visa, green card or US passport); proof of address within the consular district; statement of employment or school registration; the applicant must appear in person with the original proof of legal presence. Deletion from the consular register (Art. 36, Presidential Decree 02-405, with Arts.

190.text: employment or school registration; the applicant must appear in person with the original proof of legal presence. Deletion from the consular register (Art. 36, Presidential Decree 02-405, with Arts. 26-27): death; final return to Algeria; change of consular district; handwritten request for cancellation; absence of more than 10 years. Deletion also removes the person from the electoral roll. A fee is charged for a certificate of deletion (amount not stated).

191.title: Loi n° 02-01 du 5 février 2002 relative à l'électricité et à la distribution du gaz par canalisations
191.text: Loi n° 02-01 du 22 Dhou El Kaada 1422 correspondant au 5 février 2002 relative à l'électricité et à la distribution du gaz par canalisations. Consumer-relevant provisions by article. 1. Access to electricity and gas. Art. 61: The sector is based on third-party access to transmission and distribution networks, so eligible customers can buy directly from producers or gas suppliers; markets to open to at least 30% within three years of promulgation. Art. 62: Eligibility depends only on annual consumption; the threshold is set by regulation and is to decrease over time. Art. 65: Eligible customers, distributors and marketers have network access rights, subject to a transport or distribution toll. Art. 67: Access "ne peut être refusé que s'il y a manque avéré de capacité"; the operator concerned may appeal to the CREG. 2. Public service obligations. Art. 3: Electricity and gas distribution is a public service aiming to guarantee supply "sur l'ensemble du territoire national".

192.title: Loi n° 02-01 du 5 février 2002 relative à l'électricité et à la distribution du gaz par canalisations
192.text: concerned may appeal to the CREG. 2. Public service obligations. Art. 3: Electricity and gas distribution is a public service aiming to guarantee supply "sur l'ensemble du territoire national". Objectives include supplying non-eligible customers with fairness, continuity and price equalization; supplying identified categories of citizens and disadvantaged regions to support social cohesion; supplying any eligible customer that cannot find a supplier on acceptable economic or technical terms. Art. 4: The State compensates public service obligations after CREG's opinion, including extra costs from State-imposed contracts and costs in particular regions. 3. Connection. Art. 65: For electricity, requests go to the market operator; once accepted and verified by the system operator, the request becomes a firm supply commitment. Gas requests go to the gas transmission manager. Art. 78: Distribution concessionaires must develop networks so that customers and producers who request connection can be connected. Art. 96: Connection rights and related economic rules are set by regulation. 4. Tariffs. Art.

193.title: Loi n° 02-01 du 5 février 2002 relative à l'électricité et à la distribution du gaz par canalisations
193.text: must develop networks so that customers and producers who request connection can be connected. Art. 96: Connection rights and related economic rules are set by regulation. 4. Tariffs. Art. 97 and 99: Tariffs for non-eligible customers (electricity and gas, excluding taxes) are set by CREG and are uniform nationwide. Art. 98 and 100: These tariffs include production or supply costs, transport and distribution costs, marketing costs, permanent system costs and diversification costs; they may include energy-saving incentives. Art. 68, 70, 80: Network-use tariffs are set by CREG, must be transparent and non-discriminatory, with a uniform structure nationwide. Art. 101: Tariff revision rules are set by regulation. Art. 63: Eligible customers may negotiate prices and quantities freely; CREG publishes model contracts. Art. 64: Supply contracts for eligible customers must last at least three years. Art. 79: Distribution concessionaires supply non-eligible customers under the tariffs in Art. 97 and 99. 5. Customer protections and service quality. Art.

194.title: Loi n° 02-01 du 5 février 2002 relative à l'électricité et à la distribution du gaz par canalisations
194.text: customers must last at least three years. Art. 79: Distribution concessionaires supply non-eligible customers under the tariffs in Art. 97 and 99. 5. Customer protections and service quality. Art. 78: Concession obligations include service quality, network safety, supply-demand balance, and compliance with technical, hygiene, safety and environmental rules. Art. 113: CREG ensures competitive and transparent markets in the consumer's interest. Art. 115(5), (21), (32): CREG proposes quality standards for supply and customer service, sets administrative sanctions and indemnities payable to consumers, and publishes information to defend consumer interests. Art. 164: High-voltage lines may not cross buildings, schools, sports centres or housing; underground electricity lines and gas pipelines may not cross cultural sites or burial grounds. 6. Complaints and disputes (CREG). Art. 115(17) and (19): CREG runs a conciliation and arbitration service and handles complaints and appeals from operators, network users and customers. Art. 132: CREG organizes a conciliation service for disputes over network access, tariffs and operator remuneration. Art.

195.title: Loi n° 02-01 du 5 février 2002 relative à l'électricité et à la distribution du gaz par canalisations
195.text: handles complaints and appeals from operators, network users and customers. Art. 132: CREG organizes a conciliation service for disputes over network access, tariffs and operator remuneration. Art. 133-137: The arbitration chamber rules on disputes between operators at a party's request, except disputes over contractual rights and obligations; its decisions cannot be appealed. Art. 139: CREG decisions must be reasoned and may be challenged before the Conseil d'État. Art. 150: Sanctions must be reasoned and may be challenged in court. Art. 162: Disputes over property works affecting network installations may go to conciliation or arbitration. 7. Sanctions. Art. 141: Operators breaching technical, public service, hygiene, safety or environmental rules are liable to fines under Art. 149. Art. 142 and 146: Sworn agents record violations in reports notified to the person concerned and to CREG; the person has 15 days to respond. Art. 148: Fines capped at 3% of prior-year turnover and no more than 5 million DA; for repeat offences 5% and 10 million DA. Art. 149: For serious breaches CREG may withdraw an operating authorization temporarily (up to one year) or permanently. Art.

196.text: and no more than 5 million DA; for repeat offences 5% and 10 million DA. Art. 149: For serious breaches CREG may withdraw an operating authorization temporarily (up to one year) or permanently. Art. 151: Building or operating an installation, direct line or direct gas pipeline without authorization: 3 months to 1 year prison and/or fine of 5 to 10 million DA. Art. 152: Obstructing inspectors or refusing requested information: 3 to 6 months prison and/or fine of 50,000 to 100,000 DA; doubled on repeat. 198.title: Electricity
198.text: Algeria's electricity sector (Ministry of Energy and Renewable Energies). Capacity and coverage: Installed capacity is 26,107.20 MW. Electricity coverage is 99%, serving 12,297,856 customers. Production: Sonelgaz produces and sells electricity through its subsidiary Sonelgaz - Electricity Production, which operates and maintains generation units to standards covering maintenance, performance and occupational safety, monitors the system's operating capability and meets public service duties including supply continuity and quality, environmental regulations and the upkeep of shared facilities. Transmission: The Sonelgaz Group, through Sonelgaz - Electricity Transmission and the system operator, runs, maintains, develops and manages the national transmission network, following applicable legislation including Law No. 02-01 of February 5, 2002 relating to electricity and gas distribution by pipelines. The core aim is a continuous balance between consumption and production, with safe, reliable and efficient supply.

199.title: Minister of Energy and Renewable Energies reviews electricity production files and preparations for summer 2026
199.text: On Sunday, November 9, 2025, Minister of Energy and Renewable Energies Dr. Mourad Adjal met with senior officials from the Sonelgaz Group at the ministry, as part of monitoring the electricity production action plan and improving public service quality across all provinces. Two files were reviewed: progress on ongoing electricity production projects, and preparations for the summer 2026 season. The Minister stressed a roadmap aligned with government priorities, which put citizen service and public service quality first, saying the ministry's main focus should be hearing citizens' concerns and responding to them. After Sonelgaz officials presented, he issued directives to speed up project execution and ensure high-quality results.

200.title: Speech by the Minister of Energy and Renewable Energies Dr Mourad Adjal at the First National Conference of Officials of the Energy and Renewable Energies Sector
200.text: Speech at the First National Meeting of Energy and Renewable Energies Sector Officials (opened 15 November 2025 per the ministry homepage). Household connections: Under the President's special programs, Sonelgaz has connected over 2.4 million homes to gas and over 456,000 homes to electricity. Gas networks now reach 8.2 million customers. Electricity coverage is "99%, with more than 12.5 million subscribers". Gas coverage is 72%, with over 8.2 million subscribers. Energy supply: Summer 2025 peak demand reached 20,628 MW, 1,085 MW higher than the previous year, and demand was fully covered. Agricultural connections: More than 100,432 farms have been connected as part of the national food security program. Safety and public services: A free program to install carbon monoxide detectors in homes has installed 17 million devices, with work progressing in all provinces. Five seawater desalination plants were connected to electricity ahead of schedule, three more being studied or prepared. 1,000 electric vehicle charging points have been installed, mainly along the East-West Highway, but they will only operate once the relevant regulatory frameworks are finalized.

201.title: Speech by the Minister of Energy and Renewable Energies Dr Mourad Adjal at the First National Conference of Officials of the Energy and Renewable Energies Sector
201.text: studied or prepared. 1,000 electric vehicle charging points have been installed, mainly along the East-West Highway, but they will only operate once the relevant regulatory frameworks are finalized. Rural and remote areas: The sector is preparing a program to supply isolated and remote areas, especially in the south, through individual solar systems and off-grid photovoltaic plants (in preparation). Renewables: target of 15,000 MW of renewable capacity by 2035; the first phase, 3,200 MW, is underway in 14 provinces.

202.title: Speech of the Minister of Energy and Renewable Energies during the meeting with the Wali of Tipaza and the elected officials
202.text: Speech by the Minister of Energy and Renewable Energies, Dr. Mourad Adjal, Wilaya of Tipaza (start of 2026). Tipaza has an installed capacity "estimated at 1,170 MVA". The electricity connection rate is 99% and the gas connection rate is 88%, with ongoing efforts to strengthen networks and energy infrastructure to meet growing demand. Programmes: diversify electricity generation using solar, wind and hydropower; launch studies on green hydrogen; guide other sectors toward energy efficiency; strengthen electricity supply in isolated areas using new and renewable energies to reduce reliance on conventional sources and keep supply continuous across the province. The visit aims to assess sector performance, review project progress and listen to citizens' concerns; the Ministry says it will study and resolve energy issues raised by elected officials and executive authorities, in coordination with local authorities and relevant institutions.

203.title: Speech of the Minister of Energy and Renewable Energies during the meeting with the Wali of Bordj Badji Mokhtar and the elected officials
203.text: Speech by Minister of Energy and Renewable Energies Dr. Mourad Adjal, Bordj Badji Mokhtar, 29 December 2025. The wilaya has a 98% electricity connection rate, with network upgrades suited to the area's terrain and demand. The State will fund a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) facility intended to supply cleaner fuel at lower cost for transport and local businesses, supporting the local economy and residents' quality of life. The visit reviews progress on approved energy, infrastructure and service projects in the wilaya. The minister says the ministry will hear concerns from elected officials and local executives and review all energy-related issues raised at the wilaya level.

204.title: Job Board
204.text: Job Board, Ministry of Energy and Renewable Energies. Current openings: there are no vacant positions at this time. The ministry recruits staff when needed to strengthen its work teams and human capital. Qualifications: "Depending on the nature of the position." How to apply: submit a cover letter and CV, either through the electronic form in each job announcement or by email to meerjob@energy.gov.dz. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a job interview. The ministry commits to keeping the personal information provided confidential and protecting it.

205.title: National Energy Policy
205.text: National Energy Policy, Ministry of Energy and Renewable Energies. Context: given the global energy transition, supply diversification and growing use of renewables, Algeria treats its energy sector as a pillar of economic development and national sovereignty. A September 14, 2025 government reshuffle gave the sector new missions. Main goals: secure national energy supply over the long term; position Algeria as a reliable regional and international energy supplier, especially to African and European markets. Ministry objectives: update the regulatory framework; make the sector a driver of growth; modernize and digitize public institutions' management; develop human capital; build a balanced, sustainable, competitive energy mix; increase renewables' share and direct it toward exports; promote energy efficiency; deepen national integration in electricity and gas; expand regional partnerships; integrate into the European electricity market.

206.title: National Energy Policy
206.text: share and direct it toward exports; promote energy efficiency; deepen national integration in electricity and gas; expand regional partnerships; integrate into the European electricity market. Actions for operators include: deliver approved programs on schedule; prepare for summer peak demand; increase local content; monitor digitalization; run training programs; advance renewables, non-electric nuclear applications, energy management and pilot hydrogen production; update the national framework for electricity and gas consumption and pricing; begin reviewing the electricity and gas tariff system; meet financial planning deadlines under organic finance law No. 18-15 of 2018 (as amended); prepare performance contracts under Executive Decree No. 20-404 of 2020.

207.title: National Service - The reserve (military obligations, rights, card renewal)
207.text: Military obligations of Algerian citizens. Under Ordinance No. 76-110, Algerian citizens have four types of military obligation: national service (12 months), availability (5 years), first reserve (10 years), and second reserve (10 years). National service: Eligible citizens over 19 must complete this period. Afterward, they are discharged and receive a National Service card. Reserve: The reserve is a military status for citizens who are not on active duty or in national service. Its purpose is to reinforce the active army in wartime or during crises such as aggression, threats or disasters, helping protect national sovereignty and territorial integrity. It has three phases: availability, first reserve, and second reserve. When reservists can be recalled: Mobilization (general or partial) during war, aggression or its threat, unrest, or natural or human-caused disasters, to strengthen the units of the People's National Army; and training and refresher periods to prepare reservists for combat and familiarize them with new weapons and techniques.

208.title: National Service - The reserve (military obligations, rights, card renewal)
208.text: disasters, to strengthen the units of the People's National Army; and training and refresher periods to prepare reservists for combat and familiarize them with new weapons and techniques. Rights: State protection, equal to that of active-duty personnel; coverage for injury or illness under ANP benefits and the military pensions code; entitlements equal to those of active soldiers under applicable laws and regulations. Obligations: Report on time to assembly or regrouping centers for mobilization or for summoned training. Provide military authorities with any information they request. Notify the National Gendarmerie brigade of your residence and any change to it. Inform the National Service Center of changes in your family situation. Renew the National Service card: first renewal 3 years after issue; second renewal 5 years after the first; third (final) renewal 5 years after the second. Renewal documents: a family card (livret de famille, if married) or civil status document (if unmarried), a valid residence certificate, two ID photos, and the previous National Service card.

Lost card: a loss declaration from the Gendarmerie (or the consulate, for residents abroad), two ID photos, and a copy of the former card if available.

212.title: Ministry of Tourism and Handicrafts - homepage (investment procedure, tourist guide, crafts)
212.text: Hotel / tourism investment procedure: "يتكون ملف الاستثمار السياحي من الملف الإداري بالإضافة إلى الملف التقني" (The tourism investment file consists of an administrative file in addition to a technical file). The wilaya Directorate of Tourism and Handicrafts sends the file to the ministry, which submits it to the committee that reviews hotel plans. The committee can issue one of three decisions: preliminary approval, preliminary approval with reservations, or rejection. The investor then uses the decision to complete the file for the building permit, financing, the benefits of the National Agency for Investment Development, and the commercial register. Tourist guide profession: Governed by Executive Decree No. 06-224 of June 2006. "يعد دليلاً في السياحة كل شخص طبيعي يرافق السياح مقابل أجر" - a tourist guide is any natural person who, for pay, accompanies tourists on tourist trips or organized visits to museums, monuments, historical sites, cultural parks and tourist sites.

213.text: مقابل أجر" - a tourist guide is any natural person who, for pay, accompanies tourists on tourist trips or organized visits to museums, monuments, historical sites, cultural parks and tourist sites. Traditional crafts: "نقصد بالحرفية التقليدية أي نشاط للإنتاج أو الإبداع أو التحويل" - a traditional craft is any production, creation, transformation, art restoration, maintenance, repair or service activity carried out mainly by hand and on a permanent basis, in a fixed, mobile or stall-based form. It may be practised individually, within a craft cooperative, or within craft enterprises. The current craft activities register lists 339 activities in three fields: traditional and artistic crafts, production crafts, and service crafts.
