436.title: Renouvellement de label incubateur
436.text: Startup.dz – Renouvellement de Label Incubateur (three-step online form, Ministère de l'Économie de la Connaissance, des Start-up et des Micro-Entreprises). Step 1 – Applicant information: NIN (required); label number (required); last name and first name; role (founder/co-founder); other co-founders (optional); age; gender; wilaya; address, email, phone (required); website, Facebook, YouTube (optional). Step 2 – Incubator information: incubator name; legal form (EURL, SARL, SPA, entreprise individuelle, SNC, university incubator, association or foundation); number of employees; creation date; NIF (required; NIS conditional); copy of commercial register (required; PDF/JPG, max 10 MB); copy of statutes (required; PDF/JPG, max 10 MB); CASNOS and CNAS membership certificates (conditional); association/foundation approval (conditional); short description, "Décrivez en maximum 400 caractères votre incubateur" (required); photos of the incubator (required; PDF/PPTX); list of equipment and services offered to startups (optional).

437.title: Renouvellement de label incubateur
437.text: short description, "Décrivez en maximum 400 caractères votre incubateur" (required); photos of the incubator (required; PDF/PPTX); list of equipment and services offered to startups (optional). Step 3 – Incubation programme: presentation of the incubation programme (required); list of incubated startups or innovative projects (required; PDF); CVs of founders and/or trainers (required; PDF/JPG, max 1 MB); research and development expenses (required; PDF/PPTX); consent to share personal information (required).

438.title: Demander ou renouveler le label incubateur – FAQ
438.text: Startup.dz – Demander ou renouveler le label incubateur (overview and FAQ). Role of incubators/accelerators: discounted workspace; shared training; shared administrative and accounting services; mentors/coaches; access to funders; introductions to potential clients, including via open innovation. FAQ on the startup label framework: - Why a label: "Afin d'avoir un cadre règlementaire dédié aux startups" – giving access to tax, parafiscal and other facilities. - Innovation: required but not necessarily technological; can be architectural, disruptive or radical, and should create a competitive advantage. - Size: caps on headcount and turnover apply; the regime targets young, temporary organisations. - Ownership: at least 50% of capital held by individuals or approved investment funds; "l'indépendance des porteurs de projets est une condition essentielle" – a subsidiary of a large company does not qualify. - Growth potential: large, homogeneous market and ability to scale.

439.title: Demander ou renouveler le label incubateur – FAQ
439.text: funds; "l'indépendance des porteurs de projets est une condition essentielle" – a subsidiary of a large company does not qualify. - Growth potential: large, homogeneous market and ability to scale. - Labelling committee: representatives designated by ministries, multidisciplinary, not administrators, with sufficient professional experience in innovation or new technologies (Article 4); may call on external experts (Article 5). - Procedure: "La procédure de labélisation se fera entièrement en ligne" – no visit to an administration needed. Application pages: new incubator label – startup.dz/label-incubateur; renewal – startup.dz/renouvellement-de-label-incubateur/.

440.title: Pour les investisseurs – financement participatif, Bourse d'Alger
440.text: Startup.dz – Pour les investisseurs. Equity crowdfunding (financement participatif): raising small sums from the general public to finance projects, as donations, loans or investments; presented as a more accessible and flexible alternative to bank loans and venture capital. Equity crowdfunding was introduced by the supplementary finance law of 2020 (LFC 2020). The ministry worked with COSOB (Commission d'Organisation et de Surveillance des Opérations de Bourse, https://www.cosob.org/) on a regulatory framework for crowdfunding intermediaries. Startup compartment at the Algiers Stock Exchange (Bourse d'Alger): a dedicated startup segment was created to revitalise the exchange and give startups new funding avenues. Sociétés de capital investissement (private equity companies): the LFC 2020 removed a set of prudential rules to encourage the private sector to invest more in venture capital.

441.title: Pour les startups – Label startup, projet innovant, ASF
441.text: Startup.dz – Pour les startups (Ministère de l'Économie de la Connaissance, des Start-up et des Micro-Entreprises). Algeria Disrupt programme: a legal and regulatory framework to promote startups and accelerate their growth; it also created a public investment fund for startups (ASF) and an accelerator ("A-venture"). Label « Startup » (for companies already created): an official "passport" to state facilities for startups. Eligibility criteria: - Age: "la société ne doit pas exister depuis plus de huit (8) ans" (company no more than 8 years old). - Innovation: the business model must rely on innovative products, services, business model or idea. - Growth potential: the company must have significant growth potential. - Annual revenue: must not exceed an amount set by the national committee. - Ownership: at least 50% of share capital held by natural persons, approved investment funds, or other companies holding the startup label. - Size: no more than 250 employees. Label « Projet innovant » (before incorporation): for project leaders who have not yet created their company; grants access to benefits similar to the startup label.

442.title: Pour les startups – Label startup, projet innovant, ASF
442.text: no more than 250 employees. Label « Projet innovant » (before incorporation): for project leaders who have not yet created their company; grants access to benefits similar to the startup label. ASF (Algerian Startup Fund): public venture-capital company financing labelled startups through equity and quasi-equity, created by the Ministry of Startups with six public banks. A-venture (Algeria Venture): network of startup accelerators/incubators. FAQ notes: the label procedure is entirely online, with no need to visit an administration; the labelling committee is made up of ministry representatives with relevant experience and can call on outside experts. Label holders gain access to fiscal, parafiscal and other facilities. Startup Meetups are held every Thursday at the ministry's headquarters. Application pages: startup label – startup.dz/label-startup; renewal – startup.dz/pour-obtenir-et-renouveler-label-startup; innovative project label – startup.dz/label-projet.

443.title: Algeria Venture (A-venture) – réseau d'accélérateurs
443.text: Startup.dz – Algeria Venture (A-venture): a network of startup accelerators in Algeria, created because the country lacked sufficient incubation/acceleration infrastructure (the name plays on entrepreneurship as "une aventure"). Two main missions: - Coaching, training and support: programmes for startups, open calls for applications to select economically viable projects, and support throughout the acceleration period. - Funding and investment: helping startups find financing for innovative projects through ASF and other public and private investment funds. The first site is at the Parc des Grands Vents (Algiers), funded and built by Sonatrach, to strengthen the Greater Algiers startup ecosystem; the page states it was 90% complete and expected for early 2021, with further sites across Algeria to follow. The page offers a form to be notified when the programme launches. A-venture's own site: aventure.dz (co-working, meeting rooms, business domiciliation, mentoring).

444.title: Startup.dz – politique de confidentialité et contact du Ministère
444.text: Startup.dz is operated by the Ministère de l'Économie de la Connaissance, des Start-up et des Micro-Entreprises (MKESM), acting as data controller. Contact: Bt 46, Boulevard Mohamed V, Alger 16000, Algeria. Email: contact@mkesm.gov.dz (also the Data Protection Delegate's address). Legal framework: Law n° 18-07 of 10 June 2018 on personal data protection, as amended by Law n° 25-11 of 24 July 2025; supervised by the ANPDP (Autorité Nationale de Protection des Données à caractère Personnel), which handles complaints. Data collected: contact details (name, email, phone, address), information on your enterprise or project, and usage data (IP address, device). Purposes: operating the platform and e-services, handling label applications and accounts, answering enquiries, legal obligations, programme announcements (opt-out possible), analytics and security. Data is generally stored in Algeria; transfers abroad require prior ANPDP authorisation. Your rights: information, access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection to prospecting, complaint to the ANPDP. Policy last updated 21 June 2026.

445.title: NESDA – Création et extension de micro-entreprise (conditions et étapes)
445.text: NESDA (Agence Nationale d'Appui et de Développement de l'Entrepreneuriat, ex-ANSEJ/ANADE) – Activities. Creating a micro-enterprise – eligibility: - Age 18 to 55 years. - Has not previously benefited from any support mechanism to create a micro-enterprise. - Holds a certificate or professional qualification, and/or recognised, certified know-how. - Provides a personal financial contribution under one of the financing formulas. Phases: 1. Online registration on the digital platform, after training at an Entrepreneurship Development Center (Maison/Centre de développement de l'entrepreneuriat). 2. Project evaluation: the Agency scores risk based on feasibility, efficiency and financing; projects scoring above 50% go to the wilaya committee. 3. Presentation of the project by its holder to the wilaya Committee for the Selection, Validation and Financing of investment projects (CSVF). 4. Issuance of an eligibility and financing certificate (attestation d'éligibilité et de financement). 5. Start of activity. Appeals: a rejected project may be appealed to the committee secretariat within 15 days of notification; if rejected again, the National Appeals Committee may be seized.

446.title: NESDA – Création et extension de micro-entreprise (conditions et étapes)
446.text: 5. Start of activity. Appeals: a rejected project may be appealed to the committee secretariat within 15 days of notification; if rejected again, the National Appeals Committee may be seized. Expanding a micro-enterprise – target groups: owners previously supported by the Agency; ANGEM beneficiaries; CNAC beneficiaries; farmers, artisans, licence holders and commercial-register holders. General conditions: age 20 to 58; active during the last two years, with proof; submission of accounting results and tax declarations (G12, C20). Phases: online registration; risk-assessment scoring (above 50% → training); 5-day specialised management training at the Agency; presentation to the wilaya committee; certificate and start of the activity. Supported sectors: agriculture, construction and public works (BTPH), industry, services, fishing, irrigation (hydraulique), transport, liberal professions, and traditional industry/crafts.

447.title: NESDA Expansion – programme d'extension d'activité
447.text: NESDA Expansion – Activity Expansion Programme (Agence Nationale d'Appui et de Développement de l'Entrepreneuriat). Purpose: help micro-enterprises grow – developing the current activity (new production line, machine, complementary product, related activity) or launching a new activity. Who can apply: micro-enterprise owners, including farmers, artisans and licence/commercial-register holders; both past Agency beneficiaries and non-beneficiaries (e.g. businesses started through ANGEM or CNAC). Common conditions: age between 20 and 58; active for the last two years, with proof (accounting records or tax declarations G12, C20). Past Agency beneficiaries – same or subsidiary activity: business still registered (commercial register, artisan card or licence); loan repayments on schedule; bank and/or unremunerated loans fully repaid; owner holds all equipment the activity needs. New activity: the manager, a partner or an employee must be qualified in the target field; creation-phase loans fully repaid; business currently operating an activity created through the Agency.

448.title: NESDA Expansion – programme d'extension d'activité
448.text: New activity: the manager, a partner or an employee must be qualified in the target field; creation-phase loans fully repaid; business currently operating an activity created through the Agency. Non-beneficiaries: no expansion subsidies/advantages from other public agencies (ANGEM, CNAC); no activity-creation benefits under the AAPI; qualifications related to the activity held by the manager, a partner or a worker. Advantages: financing up to 10,000,000 DZD; 5-day entrepreneurship training; mixed (owner + Agency) or triangular (owner + Agency + bank) financing; loans with 100% interest rebate (bonification); attractive repayment terms; tax benefits under current tax legislation. Financing modes: self-financing – 100% personal; mixed – 50% personal / 50% Agency unremunerated loan; triangular – 12% to 15% personal, 15% to 18% Agency, 70% bank loan.

449.title: NESDA Expansion – programme d'extension d'activité
449.text: current tax legislation. Financing modes: self-financing – 100% personal; mixed – 50% personal / 50% Agency unremunerated loan; triangular – 12% to 15% personal, 15% to 18% Agency, 70% bank loan. Steps: 1) electronic registration on the Agency's digital platform; 2) feasibility scoring (above 50% → training); 3) 5 days of management training; 4) presentation to the wilaya Committee for the Selection, Approval and Financing of Investment Projects; 5) if approved, Eligibility and Financing Certificate, then administrative procedures with tax, social security and other services and suppliers; 6) start of the new activity.

450.title: NESDA – Formules de financement
450.text: NESDA – Financing formulas for creating and expanding micro-enterprises. - Self-financing (autofinancement): the project owner covers 100% of the investment. - Mixed financing: owner 50%, Agency 50% (unremunerated loan). - Triangular financing: owner 5% to 15%, Agency 15% to 25% (unremunerated loan), bank 70%. Contribution ratios (owner / Agency / bank): - Triangular – students and unemployed: 5% / 25% / 70% - Triangular – non-unemployed, southern regions: 10% / 20% / 70% - Triangular – non-unemployed, High Plateaus and special regions: 12% / 18% / 70% - Triangular – non-unemployed, other regions: 15% / 15% / 70% - Mixed: 50% / 50% / 0% - Self-financing: 100% / 0% / 0% Key terms: project funding up to 10,000,000 DZD; bank loans with 100% interest rebate; attractive repayment terms. Additional unremunerated loans: - Rent loan (up to 500,000 DZD): covers rent of premises or port berths for goods and service activities; excludes non-sedentary activities; granted only when the project holder applies for bank financing at the creation phase. - Operating loan (up to 1,000,000 DZD): exceptional loan for operating needs.

451.title: NESDA – Formation des porteurs de projets
451.text: NESDA – Training. Training is the foundation for creating and growing micro-enterprises. - ILO-accredited programmes: "Find Your Project Idea" (Trouver votre idée de projet – 3 days) and "Start and Improve Your Project/Business" (Créer et gérer mieux votre entreprise – 7 days); more than 107 certified trainers; post-training follow-up. - Entrepreneurship Development Centers (Centres de développement de l'entrepreneuriat): same two sessions, run with higher-education and vocational-training institutions. - Thematic sessions with public authorities: taxation and tax disputes, social security, agricultural insurance.

452.title: NESDA – Inscription au registre de commerce via le portail du CNRC
452.text: NESDA – Commercial register registration through the CNRC electronic portal. The Centre National du Registre de Commerce (CNRC) provides a dedicated electronic portal for setting up an enterprise. It provides information and procedures for creating a business, coordinated with the Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI), CASNOS (social security for non-salaried workers), CNAS (social security for salaried workers) and the Office National des Statistiques (ONS), covering commercial registration, tax, social security and economic statistics. Under Law No. 04-08 (conditions for exercising commercial activities) and Executive Decree No. 23-169, the portal handles registration, transfer and electronic receipt of documents and assigns a common identification number. Registering an establishment through the portal counts as its single registration once approved by the CNRC and confirmed by the competent authorities. Registration link: sidjilcom-entreprise.cnrc.dz/ar/accueil2

453.title: Algerian Startup Fund (ASF) – financement des startups
453.text: Algerian Startup Fund (ASF) – public venture-capital fund for startups (created by the Ministry of the Knowledge Economy, Startups and Micro-Enterprises with six public banks). Eligibility: the Startup Label is required ("Being labeled is a prerequisite to partner with ASF"). Applicants should be innovative, registered startups with a strong product vision and a dedicated team. Key criteria: "Innovation, scalability, economic impact, maturity, and team structure." Financing: equity and quasi-equity instruments suited to innovation risk; regional mechanisms with dedicated envelopes across the country; ticket sizes up to DZD 150 million per project depending on needs and maturity; post-investment support (guidance, partner network, export readiness, scaling). How to apply: 1) check eligibility; 2) obtain the Startup Label on startup.dz; 3) prepare a file covering product, team, traction and legal status; 4) apply online (asf.dz/asf/contact – "Demande d'investissement" form: full name, email, company, subject, message, privacy consent); 5) evaluation – a few weeks on average depending on volume; 6) decision. Contact: phone +213 770-534-185; email contact@asf.dz.

454.title: Ministère de l'Économie de la Connaissance, des Start-up et des Micro-Entreprises – contact
454.text: Ministry of the Knowledge Economy, Startups and Micro-Enterprises (MKESM). Mission: to "foster innovation and support startups" to build a knowledge-based economy. The official website is under development. Contact: Chemin Cherif Omar, Alger Centre 16000, Algeria. Phone: +213 023 50 52 00. Email: contact@mkesm.gov.dz (also contact@startup.dz). Bodies/platforms under the ministry linked from the site: startup.dz (labels), Algerian Startup Fund (asf.dz), Algeria Venture (aventure.dz), NESDA (nesda.dz), ANGEM (angem.dz – microcredit), ANAE (anae.dz – auto-entrepreneur), ASEP (asep.dz). Upcoming: African Startup Conference, 5–7 December 2026.

455.title: الوكالة الوطنية للمقاول الذاتي – شروط الحصول على بطاقة المقاول الذاتي
455.text: الوكالة الوطنية للمقاول الذاتي (ANAE) من نحن: الوكالة الوطنية للمقاول الذاتي مؤسسة عمومية ذات طابع إداري، تعمل تحت وصاية الوزير المكلف باقتصاد المعرفة والمؤسسات الناشئة والمؤسسات المصغرة. تهدف إلى تنظيم الأنشطة الاقتصادية الجديدة، خاصة في مجال الرقمنة، وتشجيع الشباب على العمل الحر وإدماجهم في الاقتصاد الرسمي. شروط الحصول على بطاقة المقاول الذاتي – يخضع التسجيل في السجل الوطني للمقاول الذاتي لثلاثة شروط: - السن القانونية: بلوغ السن القانونية للعمل. - الجنسية: أن يكون جزائري الجنسية ومقيمًا في الجزائر، أو أجنبيًا مقيمًا وفق التشريع المعمول به. - النشاط: أن يمارس نشاطًا مدرجًا ضمن قائمة الأنشطة المؤهلة للاستفادة من القانون الأساسي للمقاول الذاتي. "يتعين على كل شخص يطلب تسجيله... أن يستعمل وجوبًا قائمة هذه النشاطات المرجعية". قائمة الأنشطة: سبعة ميادين – الاستشارة والخبرة والتكوين؛ الخدمات الرقمية والأنشطة ذات الصلة؛ الخدمات الموجهة للأشخاص؛ الخدمات المنزلية؛ خدمات الترفيه والتسلية؛ الخدمات الموجهة للمؤسسات؛ الخدمات الثقافية والاتصال والسمعي البصري. إضافة إلى نشاط الاستيراد المصغر المحدد بالمرسوم التنفيذي رقم 25-170 (دليل الاستيراد المصغر: anae.dz/micro-importer/guide).

456.title: الوكالة الوطنية للمقاول الذاتي – شروط الحصول على بطاقة المقاول الذاتي
456.text: الخدمات الموجهة للمؤسسات؛ الخدمات الثقافية والاتصال والسمعي البصري. إضافة إلى نشاط الاستيراد المصغر المحدد بالمرسوم التنفيذي رقم 25-170 (دليل الاستيراد المصغر: anae.dz/micro-importer/guide). طلب بطاقة المقاول الذاتي عبر الخط: https://anae.dz/user/ae/register (يُدخل الاسم بالحروف اللاتينية؛ الجنسية حالياً جزائرية – "Bientôt ouvert à toutes les nationalités"؛ كلمة سر من 8 أحرف على الأقل تجمع بين حروف كبيرة وصغيرة وأرقام؛ الموافقة على معالجة المعطيات الشخصية وفق القانون 18-07). اقتراح نشاط جديد: activities.anae.dz/proposition/ مستجدات: مذكرة رقم 2024/133 المؤرخة في 01 أكتوبر 2024 – عدم إلزامية رقم التعريف الإحصائي (NIS) لممارسة نشاط المقاول الذاتي أو لفتح حساب بنكي. مذكرة رقم 2024/01 المؤرخة في 30 جانفي 2024 – تسهيل إجراءات فتح الحسابات البنكية التجارية لفائدة المقاولين الذاتيين. معلومات الاتصال: العنوان: طريق الشريف عمر، الجزائر الوسطى 16000، الجزائر. الهاتف: ‎+213 23 50 50 38 / ‎+213 23 50 57 23 / ‎+213 23 50 69 73. البريد الإلكتروني: contact@anae.dz. ساعات العمل: 09:00 - 16:00.

457.title: المواد والسلع والتجهيزات المستثناة من نشاط الاستيراد المصغر
457.text: الوكالة الوطنية للمقاول الذاتي – قائمة المواد والسلع والتجهيزات المستثناة من نشاط الاستيراد المصغر الذي يمارسه المقاول الذاتي، استناداً إلى المادة 9 من المرسوم التنفيذي رقم 25-170 المؤرخ في 28 جوان 2025: 1. السلع المحظورة والمواد الحساسة: جميع أصناف العتاد والأسلحة والذخيرة، وأنظمة الطائرات المسيّرة المحمولة، والمواد والمنتجات الكيميائية والخطرة، والمواد المتفجرة. 2. التجهيزات الحساسة: أي عتاد قد يؤدي استعماله غير المشروع إلى المساس بالأمن الوطني أو النظام العام. 3. المواد الصيدلانية: جميع المواد الصيدلانية والأجهزة والمستلزمات الطبية التي يتطلب نشاطها اعتماداً قانونياً. 4. السلع المشروطة برخصة خاصة: السلع أو المواد أو التجهيزات التي يستلزم استيرادها حيازة رخصة أو اعتماد، مع احترام دفتر الشروط الخاص بها واستيفاء المتطلبات التقنية وإجراء التحقيقات الإدارية والأمنية عند الاقتضاء. 5. الأمن والنظام العام والآداب: السلع أو المواد التي تمس بمقتضيات الأمن أو النظام العام أو الآداب العامة. 6. سلع ومواد أخرى يُمنع استيرادها (التفاصيل عبر رابط "اطّلع على التفاصيل" في الصفحة).

458.title: Liste des activités éligibles au statut d'auto-entrepreneur
458.text: ANAE – Reference list of activities eligible for the auto-entrepreneur status (every applicant must choose an activity from this list). Eight domains with codes: 1. Conseil, expertise et formation (010000): organisational and management consulting, financial analysis, socio-economic studies, technical training, health and wellness services, public relations, geographic and meteorological information services. 2. Services numériques et activités connexes (020000): software development, digital design, digital marketing, e-commerce services, online education, cloud computing, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, big data, IT systems administration, project management. 3. Services à la personne (030000): home childcare, home help for elderly or disabled people, home meal preparation, tutoring/homework support, sports and wellness coaching, gardening and landscaping, pet care, accompanying people on trips. 4. Services à domicile (040000): home assistance, repair of household appliances, computer and office equipment maintenance. 5. Loisirs et divertissement (050000): event organisation, multimedia content design, recreational activities. 6.

459.title: Liste des activités éligibles au statut d'auto-entrepreneur
459.text: repair of household appliances, computer and office equipment maintenance. 5. Loisirs et divertissement (050000): event organisation, multimedia content design, recreational activities. 6. Services aux entreprises (060000): technical and industrial work including electrical and electronic maintenance, HVAC, welding, metal structures, industrial quality analysis, industrial design, HR assistance, client technical support. 7. Services culturels, communication et audiovisuel (070000): book writing, music and singing, photography, film and video production, editing, stage lighting and sound, costume and make-up, artist promotion, modelling. 8. Micro-importation (080000): "L'activité de micro-importation" (new; governed by Executive Decree 25-170). Activities not on the list can be proposed at activities.anae.dz/proposition/.

460.title: ARPCE – Droits des abonnés
460.text: ARPCE (Autorité de Régulation de la Poste et des Communications Électroniques) – Droits des abonnés (subscriber rights). Right to redress (droit de recours): A subscriber may file a complaint with their operator, which must follow up on it. If the subscriber is dissatisfied, or the operator does not respond, the subscriber may refer the matter to the Regulatory Authority (ARPCE). Right to information: Operators must provide clear and precise information about the offers they plan to launch. Operators must inform subscribers by publishing their tariffs and general terms of service offers. Operators must inform subscribers of any change to a market offer. Operators must not harm the subscriber's moral interest. Right to privacy: - Personal data: Operators must take measures to keep the personal information they hold and process confidential, in line with applicable laws and regulations. - Confidentiality of communications: Operators must keep subscriber information and communications confidential. They may not allow monitoring of phone calls or electronic exchanges without prior authorization from the judicial authority.

461.title: ARPCE – Droits des abonnés
461.text: must keep subscriber information and communications confidential. They may not allow monitoring of phone calls or electronic exchanges without prior authorization from the judicial authority. - Protection of children and vulnerable people: Operators must provide subscribers with technological and organizational tools to restrict access to unwanted destinations or content for children or vulnerable people under their care. Quality of service: - Continuity: Operators may not interrupt services without prior authorization from ARPCE, except in duly established force majeure ("cas de force majeur dument constaté"). - Availability: Operators must keep services running 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Average cumulative downtime across the network must not exceed 24 hours per year, excluding force majeure. - Universal service: Universal service is a minimum set of services, including one or more value-added services, that must be available to the entire population at affordable prices across the national territory. Its aim is to increase the number of households with access to electronic services.

462.title: ARPCE – Faire une réclamation
462.text: ARPCE – Réclamation (complaint intake page). Description: "L'Autorité de régulation met à la disposition des utilisateurs un formulaire web pour déposer une réclamation." (The regulator provides users with a web form for filing a complaint.) Definition: "Il est entendu par une réclamation, une déclaration actant le mécontentement d'un client envers un service de télécommunication ou de la poste." (A complaint is a statement recording a customer's dissatisfaction with a telecommunications or postal service.) What is not a complaint: "Une demande de prestation de services, de clarification ou une demande d'avis" is not considered a complaint (a request for a service, a request for clarification or a request for an opinion).

463.title: ARPCE – Faire une réclamation
463.text: "Une demande de prestation de services, de clarification ou une demande d'avis" is not considered a complaint (a request for a service, a request for clarification or a request for an opinion). Prerequisite question on the form: "Avez-vous saisi votre Opérateur concernant votre réclamation ?" (Have you already contacted your operator about your complaint?) Options: "Oui, j'ai déjà saisi mon Opérateur concernant ma réclamation." / "Non, pas encore." Related (from the ARPCE FAQ and subscriber rights pages): a complaint must first be filed with the operator; if the operator does not respond within 15 days or the answer is unsatisfactory, the subscriber may refer the matter to ARPCE. ARPCE short number: 3333; email info@arpce.dz; reception Sunday to Thursday 8:00–16:30 at 1 Rue Kaddour Rahim, Hussein Dey, 16005 Alger.

464.title: ARPCE – Procédure en cas de vol (carte SIM)
464.text: ARPCE – Procedure in case of theft of a SIM card (puce de téléphonie mobile). Under Executive Decree No. 09-410 of 10 December 2009, post-paid and prepaid SIM cards count as sensitive equipment. Procedure: 1. Inform the authorities immediately. Under Article 26 of the decree, the holder must "informer immédiatement les services de sécurité territorialement compétents" and the authorities that issued the authorization (Articles 13, 17 and 20). 2. File a theft report. The subscriber must file a theft declaration (déclaration de vol) at the police station (commissariat de police) or National Gendarmerie brigade nearest to the place of the theft. 3. Notify the operator. The subscriber must give the operator a copy of the theft declaration certificate so the SIM card can be systematically suspended and blocked. Theft outside the place of activity or residence: the nearest security service must be informed without delay. The declaration is then confirmed with the Sûreté nationale or National Gendarmerie and with the relevant services of the wilaya where the activity or residence is located.

465.title: ARPCE – Procédure en cas de vol (carte SIM)
465.text: informed without delay. The declaration is then confirmed with the Sûreté nationale or National Gendarmerie and with the relevant services of the wilaya where the activity or residence is located. Related advice (ARPCE 'Conseils aux usagers'): when buying a phone, note and keep its IMEI number; it allows the device to be blocked if lost or stolen. Contact ARPCE: arpce.dz/fr/contact, short number 3333.

466.title: ARPCE – FAQ
466.text: ARPCE – Frequently asked questions (condensed). 1. Equipment requiring homologation: terminal equipment and radio installations intended to connect to the public network. 2. Checking whether homologation applies: submit an information request at the dedicated counter with the equipment's technical sheet. 3. Certificate of conformity: file a regulatory application under ARPCE Decision No. 26-97 of 31 January 2026. 4. Processing time: ARPCE must respond within two months of receiving a complete file. 5. Radio equipment requiring homologation: devices operating in GSM, UMTS, LTE and Wi-Fi bands. 6. Wi-Fi frequency and power limits (EIRP): 2400–2483.5 MHz (100 mW, indoor/outdoor); 5150–5250 MHz (200 mW, indoor); 5250–5350 MHz (200 mW, indoor/outdoor); 5470–5670 MHz (1000 mW, outdoor). 7. Verifying homologation: homologated equipment carries a permanent label reading "Homologué par l'ARPCE" and the homologation number, applied before sale. 8. Using another company's certificate: No, the certificate is nominative. 9. Fees: a file management fee of 7,140 DA (tax included), plus technical study fees depending on equipment type. 10.

467.text: sale. 8. Using another company's certificate: No, the certificate is nominative. 9. Fees: a file management fee of 7,140 DA (tax included), plus technical study fees depending on equipment type. 10. Tracking an application: ARPCE notifies applicants by email. 11. Unsatisfactory complaint with an operator: if no response comes within 15 days, or the answer is unsatisfactory, you can refer the matter to ARPCE. 12. Unannounced offer changes: operators must inform subscribers of any change affecting their subscribed offer. 13. A neighbour's relay antenna: ARPCE can conduct inspections at the customer's request, per current regulations. 14. 469.title: ARPCE – Conseils aux usagers
469.text: ARPCE – Advice to users of electronic communications and postal services. 1. Identification: "le client doit être dument identifié auprès de l'opérateur" (the customer must be properly identified with the operator). 2. SIM/USIM use: the card is for the sole personal use of its legal holder. 3. Deceased holder: heirs should go to an operator's commercial agency or sales point to terminate the deceased person's subscription. 4. IMEI: when buying a phone, note and keep its IMEI. It lets you block the device if it is lost or stolen. 5. Contracts: read subscription contracts carefully when buying a SIM card, and ask for a copy. 6. Disputes: file a complaint with the operator first. If there is no response or the response is unsatisfactory, the subscriber can refer the matter to ARPCE. 7. Approved devices: buy a phone approved (homologué) by ARPCE and bearing its 'ARPCE' label. 8. Radio wave concerns: subscribers worried about emissions from mobile antennas can file a complaint with ARPCE, which will check compliance with public exposure limits under decision n°82/SC/PC/ARPT/2015 of 09/12/2015.

473.title: SNTF – Avantages tarifaires
473.text: SNTF (Société Nationale des Transports Ferroviaires) – Fare reductions and travel cards. Children: under 4, free if carried on an accompanying adult's knees. Ages 4 to 12: half fare (50% off) with a separate seat. Carte Jeune (youth card): 20% off ticket purchases. Valid 1 year from issue. Named card for ages 15 to 28. Routes over 100 km: Algiers suburban, regional and long-distance (grandes lignes) services. Application: submit to the station master (chef de gare) a handwritten request, a civil status document (extrait d'acte de naissance) and two ID photos (one for the card, one for the file). Issued within one day. Fee: 60 DA. Carte Famille Nombreuse (large family card): 30% off, second class only. Valid 3 years. For families with at least 3 unmarried children under 18; requested by the head of family. Routes: regional and long-distance services. Application: a special form available at the station, signed by the head of family, plus photos, family record book (livret de famille), birth certificates, and an official document proving the nationality of the head of family and spouse. Issued within 10 days.

474.title: SNTF – Avantages tarifaires
474.text: the head of family, plus photos, family record book (livret de famille), birth certificates, and an official document proving the nationality of the head of family and spouse. Issued within 10 days. Fee: 100 DA regardless of how many cards are issued; duplicates charged per card. Carte 3ème Âge (senior card): 20% off each ticket. Valid for life. Eligibility: women 55 and older, men 60 and older. Routes over 100 km: Algiers suburban, regional and long-distance. Application at ticket counters with an ID document and one photo. Issued within one day. Fee: 60 DA. Persons with reduced mobility: free or reduced tickets depending on disability rate, on presentation of the card issued by the wilaya Social Action services (DAS). Ordinary tickets: one-way full fare; for trips of at least 200 km interrupted en route, the ticket is valid 5 days (Fridays and holidays included) if endorsed at the station where the journey was interrupted. Round trip: 20% off for trips over 400 km (aller-retour), valid 2 months. Subscriptions (abonnements): - Ordinary (named, 35% off, second class, routes up to 200 km): 1 month, 3 months or 1 year.

475.title: SNTF – Avantages tarifaires
475.text: Round trip: 20% off for trips over 400 km (aller-retour), valid 2 months. Subscriptions (abonnements): - Ordinary (named, 35% off, second class, routes up to 200 km): 1 month, 3 months or 1 year. Monthly includes 15 free days of travel; annual includes 5 free months. Apply on the rail form at least 8 days ahead at any station, with ID, a photocopy of ID, and payment. Consignment fee: 50 DA. Duplicates charged per card. - Weekly suburban (Annaba, Constantine, Oran only): 30% off, 1 week. - Monthly suburban (Annaba, Constantine, Oran only): 40% off, 1 month. - Carte Verte (Algiers suburban railcars): 30% off weekly; 40% off monthly, quarterly, semi-annual and annual. Annual cards can be paid in 3 instalments. - Half-fare cards (cartes demi-tarif): issued on request at the Regional Rail Directorate headquarters, for 3, 6 or 12 months; annual cards payable in 3 instalments. Card A: half-fare tickets in first or second class at the traveller's choice. Card B: half-fare tickets in second class only. Group travel: - Ordinary groups of 10 or more on a round trip: 30% off, for trips up to 300 km round trip. Children 4 to 12 pay half the adult price.

476.title: SNTF – Avantages tarifaires
476.text: Card B: half-fare tickets in second class only. Group travel: - Ordinary groups of 10 or more on a round trip: 30% off, for trips up to 300 km round trip. Children 4 to 12 pay half the adult price. - Sports groups (affiliated with national or foreign federations): 30% off for 10+, 40% off for 31+, 50% off for 61+. - Summer camps (colonies de vacances): groups of 10+ under age 21 get 50% off full single fares; 75% when organised at the exclusive cost of communes or charitable organisations. Upgrades: to move to a higher class, declare it to the train chief or inspector first and pay the difference between two single fares; otherwise the traveller is irregular. Ticket checks and irregular travel: tickets must be shown on request and returned at the end of the trip (or exchanged for a service note). A traveller is irregular if they have no ticket, an expired or altered ticket, no return coupon, travel beyond the ticket's distance/route without notice, or travel in a higher class without notice. Without fraud, the traveller can avoid prosecution by paying a flat indemnity plus the fare difference on the spot.

478.title: CREG – التسعيرة (Tarifs de l'électricité et du gaz)
478.text: لجنة ضبط الكهرباء والغاز (CREG) – التسعيرة. Electricity and gas tariffs page. Legal basis: tariffs are governed by Law No. 02-01 of 5 February 2002 on electricity and gas distribution through pipelines (القانون رقم 02-01 المؤرخ في 5 فبراير 2002). Setting authority: CREG set electricity and gas tariffs under decision No. D/22-15/CD of 29 December 2015. The tariffs took effect on 1 January 2016 and are expressed excluding taxes (hors taxes). Uniformity: the tariffs are "موحدة في جميع انحاء التراب الوطني" (uniform throughout the national territory). Cost components: for electricity, the tariff covers production, transport, distribution and marketing; for natural gas, transport, distribution and marketing. The detailed tariff tables (tiers and prices per kWh / thermie) are published on the page as images: electricity table https://creg.gov.dz/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Capture-5.png and gas table https://creg.gov.dz/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Capture-2.png (not transcribed here). CREG also offers an online bill estimator (تقدير فاتورتك) at https://mouhakat.creg.dz/. Contact: CREG, Section 04, Groupe de propriété 788, Zone d'activité, Immeuble Chéraga, Alger.

480.title: CREG – تقديم طعن (Recours des consommateurs)
480.text: تقديم طعن لدى لجنة ضبط الكهرباء والغاز (CREG) المرجع القانوني: تنص المادة 115 من القانون رقم 02-01 المؤرخ في 5 فبراير 2002 على أن اللجنة تسهر على حماية مصالح المستهلكين وصون حقوقهم في التزويد وجودة الخدمة واستمراريتها، وتستقبل شكاواهم وطلبات الطعن وتدرسها وفق الإجراءات المعمول بها. 1. الحالات التي يمكن فيها التوجه إلى اللجنة (عند وجود نزاع مع الموزِّع): - عدم معالجة طلب ربط أو تعديله، أو التأخر في إنجازه. - عدم معالجة طلب تحويل منشأة، أو التأخر في إنجازه. - عدم معالجة مشكلة تتعلق بالانقطاع أو الإصلاح أو السلامة. - الاعتراض على فاتورة الطاقة (مبلغ مفرط، مؤشر خاطئ، استهلاك غير صحيح، إلخ). - طلب تعديل عقد التزويد (التعريفة، القدرة، التدفق، إلخ). - طلب إعادة التزويد بعد قطعه بسبب عدم التسديد. - انخفاض التوتر أو الضغط. - المشاكل المرتبطة بالعداد. - حقوق المتابعة (الحصة الجزئية). - التعويض عن الحوادث. 2. الإجراءات المسبقة لدى الموزِّع: يجب تقديم كل شكوى تقنية أو تجارية أو إدارية أولاً إلى موزِّع الكهرباء والغاز وفق إجراءاته الداخلية لمعالجة الشكاوى المعتمدة من اللجنة. الموزِّع: الشركة الجزائرية لتوزيع الكهرباء والغاز (SADEG)، مبنى 500 مكتب، الطريق رقم 38، وادي قسنطينة، الجزائر؛ الهاتف 021.83.55.00؛ الموقع www.sonelgaz-distribution.dz.

481.title: CREG – تقديم طعن (Recours des consommateurs)
481.text: الشكاوى المعتمدة من اللجنة. الموزِّع: الشركة الجزائرية لتوزيع الكهرباء والغاز (SADEG)، مبنى 500 مكتب، الطريق رقم 38، وادي قسنطينة، الجزائر؛ الهاتف 021.83.55.00؛ الموقع www.sonelgaz-distribution.dz. يمكن الاستعانة بإحدى جمعيات حماية المستهلك (القائمة على موقع وزارة التجارة). 3. متى يمكن تقديم الطعن؟ إذا لم تتلقَّ ردّاً من الموزِّع في أجل أقصاه ثلاثة (03) أشهر، أو إذا كان الرد غير مرضٍ. يجب إرفاق الطعن بالوثائق الثبوتية، مثل نسخ جميع المراسلات الموجهة إلى الموزِّع وردوده إن وُجدت. 4. كيفية تقديم الطعن: عبر الإنترنت بملء الاستمارة الإلكترونية أو عبر منصة "إلتماس" (iltimess.creg.dz)؛ أو بتحميل الاستمارة الورقية وإيداعها بمقر اللجنة (من الأحد إلى الخميس، 09:00–16:00)، أو إرسالها بالبريد إلى: لجنة ضبط الكهرباء والغاز، القسم 04، المجموعة الملكية 788، منطقة النشاط، عمارة الشراقة، الجزائر؛ أو بالفاكس 028 91 03 02؛ أو بالبريد الإلكتروني recours@creg.gov.dz. 5. مسار المعالجة: تدرس اللجنة القبول والاختصاص في أجل أقصاه ثلاثة (03) أيام عمل، ثم تُعلمكم إن كان الطعن خارج الاختصاص أو غير مقبول (عدم استنفاد الإجراءات المسبقة، ملف ناقص، نزاع أمام القضاء). في حال القبول تطلب اللجنة من الموزِّع التوضيحات وتدعوه إلى الرد خلال خمسة عشر (15) يوماً.

482.title: CREG – تقديم طعن (Recours des consommateurs)
482.text: تُعلمكم إن كان الطعن خارج الاختصاص أو غير مقبول (عدم استنفاد الإجراءات المسبقة، ملف ناقص، نزاع أمام القضاء). في حال القبول تطلب اللجنة من الموزِّع التوضيحات وتدعوه إلى الرد خلال خمسة عشر (15) يوماً. إذا كانت حجج الموزِّع مبررة تُرسل اللجنة رسالة توضيحية وتغلق الملف؛ وإذا كانت غير مبررة تطالبه بالامتثال، فإن رفض تتخذ اللجنة قراراً لصالحكم يُبلَّغ للطرفين. يمكن للجنة جمع الأطراف لتسوية ودية. يبقى لكل طرف حق اللجوء إلى الجهات القضائية المختصة. 6. الاتصال: الهاتف +213 28 91 03 01 / +213 28 91 03 02؛ contact@creg.gov.dz؛ الطعون recours@creg.gov.dz.

483.title: CCP / e-CCP - Algérie Poste
483.text: Algérie Poste – CCP (compte courant postal) and e-CCP services for individuals. 1. CCP account Opening an account (individuals): provide a copy of a valid ID document and either a residence certificate (certificat de résidence) or a certificate of presence in the military or paramilitary corps (attestation de présence). Submit the account application form "CH1" and sign the two signature specimens on form "CH 25", available at the post office. Legal entities must go to the main receipt office (recette principale) of the chef-lieu de wilaya or the company service. Changing address: submit a request on plain paper or form "CH18", with a copy of valid ID and a residence certificate for the new address (or a certificate of presence for military and paramilitary personnel). Changing the account name: use form "CH4" with supporting documents: name change – copy of the court judgment; spelling correction of a name or first name – copy of the court judgment; marriage of a woman – copy of the marriage certificate; divorce – copy of the court judgment. Changing signature: sign the two "CH 25" specimens with the new signature.

484.title: CCP / e-CCP - Algérie Poste
484.text: – copy of the court judgment; marriage of a woman – copy of the marriage certificate; divorce – copy of the court judgment. Changing signature: sign the two "CH 25" specimens with the new signature. Cash withdrawals (paiements à vue): withdrawals can be made at any post office using a CCP cheque or form "SFP1", together with the CCP withdrawal card. Withdrawals are capped at 200,000 DA per day. Above 200,000 DA, the client must place a fund reservation, which is fulfilled within 48 hours at most. Withdrawals on sight without balance check: up to 30,000 DA can be withdrawn at the office holding the signature specimen ("CH 25 bis"), in exchange for a cheque payable to the office head, by the account holder or their authorised representative (mandataire). Deposits (versements): made at any post office with valid ID, using CCP mandats "1418" or accelerated deposit ("VAC"). Balance inquiry: at any post office by submitting form "SFP1" with ID, or by presenting a cheque and the account holder's ID. Balance can also be checked by phone (dial "15-30"), by SMS to "603", or online via the e-CCP service. Account statement (relevé): requested at any post office or online via the e-CCP site.

485.title: CCP / e-CCP - Algérie Poste

Receiving a cheque book: the client is notified by an arrival notice sent to their home address, or by SMS if subscribed to SMS notifications. 2. e-CCP account The web service lets users check their CCP balance, view and download their account statement, change their confidential code, and order a cheque book.

487.title: CREG – Droits et Obligations des consommateurs
487.text: CREG (Commission de Régulation de l'Électricité et du Gaz) – Rights and obligations of electricity and gas consumers (owners or tenants of a dwelling) towards the distributor. Your rights as an owner or tenant: - Obtain an electricity or gas connection where a network exists. - Be welcomed, advised and assisted by the distributor. - Receive four invoices per year. - Be informed of connection conditions and timelines, tariffs and payment methods. - Be informed of internal and external appeal (recours) options. - Receive advance notice of scheduled outages, including dates and times. - Receive answers to all your complaints. - Be compensated if your equipment is damaged by outages or voltage drops. - Be compensated when the distributor's structures or lines cross your property. Your obligations toward the distributor: - Pay your energy bill by the due date printed on it. - Keep your indoor installations compliant with safety standards and good practice. - Give the distributor easy, permanent access to your meter and installations. - Refuse any fraudulent connections made from your installations. - Contact the distributor before starting work near its facilities.

Contact CREG: +213 28 91 03 01 / 02, contact@creg.gov.dz. Complaints (recours): recours@creg.gov.dz.

489.title: CREG – Comment lire votre facture
489.text: CREG – How to read your electricity and gas bill (Sonelgaz / SADEG). Invoice header: invoice number and issue date; consumption-place reference (a unique number assigned by the distributor) and consumption address; expected date of the next meter reading. Distributor (SADEG – Société Algérienne de Distribution de l'Électricité et du Gaz): logo and share capital, responsible distribution directorate and local commercial agency; identifiers RC, NIS, NIF, RIB and RIP. Customer: customer number and name of the consumption-place owner; RC and NIF for non-household customers. Call centre: 33 03, for assistance, breakdowns, complaints and information requests. Billing period: one quarter, covering three months of consumption. Meter and tariff codes: the meter number is the last four digits shown at the bottom of the meter. Electricity: 54M (household, four tiers) and 54NM (non-household, three tiers). Gas: 23M (household, four tiers) and 23NM (non-household, three tiers). Subscribed power (PMD) and flow (DMD): PMD is chosen from standard values – single-phase 220 V at 4, 6 or 12 kW; three-phase 380 V at 20, 40, 60 or 80 kW.

490.title: CREG – Comment lire votre facture
490.text: and 23NM (non-household, three tiers). Subscribed power (PMD) and flow (DMD): PMD is chosen from standard values – single-phase 220 V at 4, 6 or 12 kW; three-phase 380 V at 20, 40, 60 or 80 kW. DMD is the hourly gas flow: 16 Nm³/h on a low-pressure network, or 25 Nm³/h on a medium-pressure network. Coefficient: electricity 1; gas: the calorific value (PCS), which converts cubic metres to thermies (Th). Meter readings: old and new indexes, ignoring decimals. Letter beside them: R – actual reading by the distributor's agent; E – estimate based on consumption history (meter faulty or inaccessible); M – special reading outside the billing cycle requested by the customer (e.g. after a move). Consumption tiers (progressive tariff): household electricity – up to 125 kWh, 125–250 kWh, 250–1,000 kWh, above 1,000 kWh; household gas – up to 1,125 Th, 1,125–2,500 Th, 2,500–7,500 Th, above 7,500 Th. 494.title: CREG – Demander une information (FAQ consommateurs)
494.text: CREG – Consumer FAQ on electricity and gas. Connections (raccordement): - The distributor normally carries out connection works, from receipt of the request until commissioning. Alternatively, the applicant can use a company approved by the distributor under a supervision contract. - A simple connection (branchement simple) applies if the property is within 25 m of the electricity network or 20 m of the gas network. Beyond that, a network extension is needed. - Applicants submit a request with a copy of ID and proof of occupancy of the premises. A technical study is followed by a quote (devis), valid for two months. Works start after payment and the necessary administrative approvals. - For gas, the meter is installed only after satisfactory leak tests and a conformity certificate from the installer. - Simple connections take up to 10 days. Extension timelines are given in the quote. Power and flow: electricity power is reserved by the distributor based on your needs, in kW. Low-voltage customers choose from values set by CREG decision D/11-13/CD (26 September 2013). Maximum gas flow for low-pressure customers is set by CREG decision D/04-13/CD (26 September 2013).

495.title: CREG – Demander une information (FAQ consommateurs)
495.text: kW. Low-voltage customers choose from values set by CREG decision D/11-13/CD (26 September 2013). Maximum gas flow for low-pressure customers is set by CREG decision D/04-13/CD (26 September 2013). Meter reading: meters are read quarterly for low-voltage and low-pressure customers, and monthly for commercial and industrial customers. The meter number is the last four digits shown on the device. Bills and payment: bills include a fixed fee (metering, billing, reading), charges for the power made available, energy consumption and State taxes. Payment options: cash or cheque at a commercial agency or post office; bank or postal account transfer; direct debit; or online via Edahabia, CIB or the WIMPAY-BNA app. Low-voltage and low-pressure bills are due within 15 days, after which supply may be cut without notice. Commercial and industrial bills are due within one month, after which formal notice is given before cutting supply. Reconnection requires payment of arrears plus cut-off and reconnection fees. Where to get help: your supplier's commercial agency or Sonelgaz Distribution (SADEG); consumer protection associations (list on the Ministry of Commerce website); CREG.

496.text: and reconnection fees. Where to get help: your supplier's commercial agency or Sonelgaz Distribution (SADEG); consumer protection associations (list on the Ministry of Commerce website); CREG. Filing a complaint with CREG: possible if you are dissatisfied with how your request was handled, or if the distributor has not responded within three months. Submit by hand at CREG headquarters (Sunday to Thursday, 9:00–16:00), by post, by fax, by email to recours@creg.gov.dz, or through the online form. Acknowledgment of receipt within 3 days; processing time depends on the complaint's nature and complexity.

497.text: CREG – State support for electricity consumers in the South and High Plateaus. Purpose: under the State's policy of supporting populations in the South, electricity consumption reductions apply to low- and medium-voltage customers in 13 wilayas. Covered wilayas – South (10): Adrar, Laghouat, Biskra, Béchar, Tamanrasset, Ouargla, Illizi, Tindouf, El Oued and Ghardaïa. High Plateaus (3): Djelfa, El Bayadh and Naâma. Support levels: 1. Legal basis: Article 137 of Law No. 16-14 (Finance Law for 2017). 2. Non-agricultural economic subscribers (low and medium voltage): reduced rate on consumption up to 200,000 kWh per year; consumption above that is billed at the regular price. Same legal basis. 3. 499.title: CREG – Dangers of Gas Leaks
499.text: CREG – Dangers of gas leaks (advice and safety). Improper use of natural gas can cause serious accidents. A gas leak can cause explosions and fires. Properties of natural gas: it is invisible; it is asphyxiating; it is explosive; it is odorised, so a leak can be detected by smell. If you smell gas, do not: create a flame or spark; smoke; use any phone at home, landline or mobile; light a match; use the doorbell (knock on the door instead); turn on light switches. What to do in case of a leak: 1. Close the main gas valve. 2. Open doors and windows to ventilate the home. 3. Evacuate the premises immediately. 4. Call emergency services from outside. Safety tips: keep the main gas valve accessible; replace the cooker's connection hoses at the end of their recommended usage period; close the main valve when gas will not be used for long periods; have the installation checked regularly by a professional and make sure the pipes are sealed. Other CREG safety topics: electricity hazards; dangers of carbon monoxide (CO). Contact CREG: +213 28 91 03 01 / 02, contact@creg.gov.dz. Sonelgaz distribution call centre: 33 03.

502.title: SNTF – Services en gares
502.text: SNTF – Services in stations. Opening hours: stations serve passengers every day of the week, including public holidays. Some close overnight, between the last arriving train and the first departing one. Staff assistance: station personnel help travellers prepare their trips, with information, bookings (réservations), ticket sales and complaints (réclamations). Accessibility: current stations offer easy access to the waiting hall and platforms for people with reduced mobility (PMR). Prayer facilities: most stations have prayer rooms and a restroom set up for ablutions. Refreshments: most stations have snack bars, and some long-distance and regional trains have dining cars (Restau RAIL). Free on-board amenities: comfort and sleeper trains offer tea, mineral water, newspapers, breakfast and wipes, depending on class. SNTF network (from homepage): about 4,498 km of track covering 30 wilayas; more than a hundred passenger stations; train types: suburban (banlieue), regional, long-distance (grandes lignes) and freight. Contact: 21-23 Boulevard Mohamed V, Alger; (213) 21 71 15 10; contact@sntf.dz.

503.title: SNTF – À bord du train
503.text: SNTF – On-board services. Comfort: SNTF is modernising its fleet to international standards. Air conditioning is provided on long-distance and regional trains, and newer units serve the Algiers suburban lines. The new long-distance Coradia train is bi-mode diesel/electric (25 kV), up to 160 km/h, 6 cars, 254 seats including 60 in first class, with accessibility for persons with reduced mobility. Information systems: suburban and intercity trains have audio-visual displays showing stations, destinations, time and outside temperature. Staff: reception and assistance agents from the subsidiary SNTF Rail-Services provide travel information, help passengers and oversee safety and comfort. About 222 ticket inspectors (contrôleurs) and 375 train chiefs (chefs de train) work across the network; inspectors check tickets, train chiefs handle pre-departure safety checks and passenger safety. Restrooms: long-distance units have accessible restrooms for elderly passengers, pregnant women and people with disabilities. Cleaning: electric units are cleaned daily at a dedicated facility (with Stadler); diesel trains are cleaned before each departure.

504.title: SNTF – À bord du train
504.text: elderly passengers, pregnant women and people with disabilities. Cleaning: electric units are cleaned daily at a dedicated facility (with Stadler); diesel trains are cleaned before each departure. Food and drink: kiosks at most stations, plus restaurant cars on long-distance routes, some items by trolley service. Complimentary items (tea, mineral water, newspapers, breakfast) on certain classes, wipes on sleeper and couchette trains. Safety equipment: CO2 fire extinguishers, first-aid kits, stretchers, alarm signals. Why take the train (homepage): group travel (54 seats per car), baggage tolerance, sleepers on long trips, buffet, service every day of the year, on-board toilets, fare reductions. 505.title: ARPCE – Portabilité des Numéros Mobiles
505.text: ARPCE – Mobile number portability (Portabilité des Numéros Mobiles, PNM) project. Legal definition: Law No. 18-04 of 10 May 2018 setting the general rules for post and electronic communications defines number portability as the "possibilité pour un abonné de conserver son numéro lorsqu'il change d'opérateur" (the possibility for a subscriber to keep their number when changing operator). Purpose: portability is an effective way to increase competition in the electronic communications market. Public consultation: on 29 July 2021, ARPCE launched a public consultation with the three mobile operators on the practical, technical, legal, organisational and pricing conditions for mobile number portability in Algeria. Regulatory texts: - Executive Decree No. 21-199 of 11 May 2021 setting the conditions and procedures for implementing mobile number portability. - Decision No. 18/SP/PC/ARPCE/2021 of 27 June 2021 setting the practical implementation rules. - Decision No. 37/SP/PC/ARPCE/2022 of 13 July 2022. - Decision No. 55/SP/PC/ARPCE/2022 of 29 August 2022. ARPCE lists PNM under its 'Grands Dossiers' (major files) section as a project.

506.title: IDOOM ADSL – Algérie Télécom
506.text: Algérie Télécom – IDOOM ADSL (home internet for individuals). Overview: Algérie Télécom offers unlimited internet through IDOOM ADSL packages, with speeds up to 20 Mbps ("Enjoy unlimited Internet access with IDOOM ADSL!"). Subscriptions can be made online or at a local store (agence commerciale). Plans and prices (per month): 10 Mbps – 1,600 DZD; 15 Mbps – 1,999 DZD; 20 Mbps – 2,599 DZD. (A separate price list on the page shows monthly rates of 1,600, 2,000, 2,200 and 2,400 DZD without speed labels.) Plans of 15 Mbps and above include free access to Dzair Play, Algérie Télécom's video-on-demand service. Higher speeds: ADSL cannot exceed 20 Mbps for technical reasons. Idoom VDSL offers 50 Mbps, and Idoom Fibre offers up to 1 Gbps. Choosing a plan: consider the number of simultaneous users, main uses (downloads, streaming, data transfer) and line eligibility. An eligibility test checks your line's maximum speed; it requires your landline number. Subscribing: apply online through the Online Request form or at a local store. Required documents: a copy of your ID, proof of address, and a completed, signed form.

507.title: IDOOM ADSL – Algérie Télécom
507.text: requires your landline number. Subscribing: apply online through the Online Request form or at a local store. Required documents: a copy of your ID, proof of address, and a completed, signed form. Every subscription carries a 12-month commitment, during which you cannot switch to a lower offer. The modem is not included and must be bought separately at points of sale. Recharging and paying bills: online payment with Edahabia or CIB cards, or recharge cards and vouchers from stores or approved resellers. Other channels: indirect points of sale (kiosks, cybercafés, tobacco shops), the website and official app, BaridiMob, the WIMPAY-BNA app, and calling 1500 from a landline or mobile. Bills can be paid at a store, the post office, or through your Customer Space. If you cannot pay, Algérie Télécom offers a payment schedule (échéancier). If your phone bill is under 3,000 DZD, you can still recharge your internet subscription and reactivate it. Business customers: IDOOM ADSL is for personal customers only; businesses can choose Idoom ADSL Pro, Idoom Fibre Pro or Moohtarif. Support: social networks, a local store, or call 12 from a landline or mobile.

508.title: Customer Space – Algérie Télécom
508.text: Algérie Télécom – Customer Space (Espace client). The Customer Space is an online portal where subscribers manage their services. It covers Idoom Fixe (landline), Idoom ADSL, Idoom Fibre and Idoom 4G LTE; each customer on these plans can create a secure personal space. Services available: manage your subscription; track your consumption; recharge your internet account; learn about online e-payment; view, download and pay your landline (fixe) bills; check subscription expiry dates; follow recharge operations; view your personal information. How to access it: 1. Go to the account section and open the menu. 2. Click 'Customer space'. 3. Log in according to your subscription type: Idoom Fixe, ADSL or Fibre, or Idoom 4G LTE. 4. Follow the steps on screen. Forgotten password: in the Customer space, click 'Forget password?'; a renewal email will be sent to your email address. Assistance: contact your nearest store (agence commerciale), or call 12 from a landline or mobile phone to reach a call-centre advisor. Internet can also be recharged by calling 1500.

509.title: CREG – Making an Appeal
509.text: CREG – Making an appeal (consumer recourse) – English version. Purpose: under Article 115 of Law No. 02-01 of 5 February 2002, CREG protects consumers' rights regarding the supply, quality and continuity of electricity and gas service. It receives and processes complaints and appeals under its published procedures. When to contact CREG – disputes with your distributor, such as: delayed or unprocessed requests for connection, modification or relocation of facilities; unaddressed outages, repairs or safety issues; billing disputes (excessive amounts, incorrect meter readings, cumulative consumption); requests to change the supply contract (tariff, power or flow rate); reconnection after disconnection for non-payment; voltage or pressure drops, metering issues, follow-up rights and compensation for incidents. Before contacting CREG: submit your complaint first to the distributor (Sonelgaz – Distribution) under its internal complaint procedure approved by CREG. You may also consult a consumer protection association. When to appeal: if you receive no response within a maximum of two months (the Arabic version of the page states three months), or the response is unsatisfactory.

510.title: CREG – Making an Appeal
510.text: a consumer protection association. When to appeal: if you receive no response within a maximum of two months (the Arabic version of the page states three months), or the response is unsatisfactory. Include supporting documents, such as copies of your letters to the distributor and any replies. How to submit: online via the Iltimess platform (iltimess.creg.dz) or the online form; in person at CREG headquarters, Sunday to Thursday, 9:00 to 16:00; by mail to CREG, Section N°04 lot n°788 Zone d'activité Amara, Cheraga, Algiers; by fax 028 91 03 02; by email recours@creg.gov.dz. If outside CREG's competence, you receive a letter saying so. 3. If admissible, CREG asks the distributor for explanations and gives it up to 15 days to respond. 5. If the distributor's position is valid, CREG closes the case and explains why. 6.

512.title: COSOB – L'ouverture d'un compte titres
512.text: COSOB (Commission d'Organisation et de Surveillance des Opérations de Bourse) – Guide: opening a securities account (compte titres). 1. Open a cash account: securities (shares, bonds, SICAV shares, FCP units, Treasury securities and financial products) must be bought or sold through a "teneur de compte-conservateur habilité par la COSOB" (custodian account-keeper approved by COSOB). You open a cash account there: a current account for individuals or a business account for legal entities. 2. Open a securities account: it records your trades and all events affecting your holdings (subscriptions, allocations, coupons, redemptions). Individuals: before opening, the custodian verifies your identity, your address, and that you have the legal capacity and status needed. Legal entities: the custodian verifies that the representative holds valid authority. Documents: you complete an account opening form and sign an account agreement ("convention de compte") in two copies; you keep one copy. The cash and securities accounts operate together: buying securities credits your securities account and debits your cash account; selling does the reverse. 3.

513.title: COSOB – L'ouverture d'un compte titres
513.text: in two copies; you keep one copy. The cash and securities accounts operate together: buying securities credits your securities account and debits your cash account; selling does the reverse. 3. Place orders: a signed buy or sell order is submitted to your custodian with all information needed for proper execution; it also authorises the corresponding movements in your cash and securities accounts. 4. Monitor your transactions: the custodian must provide an execution notice (avis d'opéré) confirming your order was carried out, and a periodic account statement showing your holdings in quantities and values. Minimum contents of the account agreement: identity of the signatories (and how authorised persons are identified and informed); services covered and categories of securities; the custodian's fees; the agreement's duration; the custodian's confidentiality obligations; characteristics of orders, how they are sent and how the client is informed of execution; how the client receives information on movements, account statements and other regulatory information.

514.title: COSOB – Investir en bourse
514.text: COSOB – Guide: Investing on the stock exchange (Investir en bourse). The stock exchange: the Algiers exchange (Bourse d'Alger) is a regulated market where companies raise capital and investors place savings. Created by Legislative Decree No. 93-10 of 23 May 1993, as amended. Three bodies: COSOB (market regulator), SGBV (Société de Gestion de la Bourse des Valeurs, manages the Bourse d'Alger), and Algérie Clearing (central depository, settlement and clearing). Products traded: shares (actions) – rights to information, voting at general meetings, dividends, preferential subscription, liquidation proceeds and bonus shares; dividends are set by the general meeting and not guaranteed. Bonds (obligations) – the investor lends to the issuer, which pays interest at a rate fixed at issuance and repays principal at maturity; types include corporate bonds and State bonds (OAT) with maturities of 7, 10 and 15 years. Other securities: investment certificates, voting-right certificates, participating securities, convertible bonds, bonds with subscription warrants.

515.title: COSOB – Investir en bourse
515.text: (OAT) with maturities of 7, 10 and 15 years. Other securities: investment certificates, voting-right certificates, participating securities, convertible bonds, bonds with subscription warrants. Advantages and risks: possible capital gains and tax exemptions on income and gains; risks include capital losses, limited market liquidity, company bankruptcy (shares) and counterparty risk (bonds). Buying and selling: individuals cannot trade directly; they must go through an approved Intermediary in Stock Market Operations (IOB); State bonds also involve Treasury Specialists (SVT). Primary market subscriptions are handled by banks and IOBs. Investors must open a securities account linked to a cash account, with a valid ID, a completed account opening form and a signed account agreement in two copies. Orders: an order is an instruction to the IOB stating direction (buy/sell), the security, quantity, any price limit, validity period and the investor's details. The IOB checks that the investor has the securities or funds.

516.title: COSOB – Investir en bourse
516.text: to the IOB stating direction (buy/sell), the security, quantity, any price limit, validity period and the investor's details. The IOB checks that the investor has the securities or funds. Types: limit orders; market orders; day orders (one session); open-ended orders (until end of the current calendar month); time-limited orders (up to 30 days); good-till-executed orders (up to three calendar weeks); all-or-nothing orders (temporarily suspended); unconditional orders (partial execution allowed). Execution: shares and corporate bonds trade on Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday; State bonds (OAT) trade Sunday through Thursday. Trades are executed electronically by fixing (one price per security per session). Block trades at the end of each session. Settlement at J+3 for securities and J+1 for OATs through Algérie Clearing. Securities are dematerialised and held in securities accounts by account keepers.

Baggage incidents (missing or damaged bags): before leaving the airport, report the problem at the airport baggage complaints service (Litige bagages). Liability limits for mishandled baggage are set out in the General Conditions of Carriage. 3. 520.title: Air Algérie – Lost and damaged baggage
520.text: Air Algérie – Lost, delayed and damaged baggage. Lost baggage: before leaving the arrival airport, contact Air Algérie's baggage service and present the baggage receipt (tag) issued at check-in. If the reported bag is not found within 2 days, send a complete list of its contents (one list per bag) and all required baggage identification tags. Missing items from baggage: provide the airport service in charge with all required documents and complete the appropriate form to help the search. Declare missing items within 3 days after the flight. Valuables: Air Algérie disclaims responsibility for loss or damage to valuables transported without prior declaration. Compensation and liability limits are set out in the General Conditions of Carriage (Conditions Générales de Transport). Claims can also be filed via https://doleances.airalgerie.dz/ (see Air Algérie claims page). Contact center Algeria: +213 21 98 63 63, short code 3302.

521.title: Air Algérie – Piece Concept (franchise bagages)
521.text: Air Algérie – Free baggage allowance (Piece Concept). Air Algérie offers a free checked baggage allowance on all flights. The allowance depends on the route, the cabin class (Economy, Business or First) and the passenger's loyalty card status at check-in. Confirm your allowance at booking or on your e-ticket. Reading your e-ticket: "1Pc" = one checked bag up to 23 kg, plus one free cabin bag. "2Pc" = two checked bags up to 23 kg each, plus one free cabin bag. Checked bag limits: maximum size 158 cm (length + width + depth); maximum weight 23 kg. Children (2–11): same allowance as adults. Infants (under 2): one checked bag of up to 10 kg; a parent or guardian can also check one stroller or car seat free of charge. Reduced mobility: passengers can check a fully foldable wheelchair, plus splints or crutches. Excess baggage: bags over 23 kg and up to 32 kg are charged according to a published tariff. Bags over 32 kg are not accepted at check-in and must be shipped as cargo. Oversized bags over 158 cm but no more than 203 cm can be checked if they fit in the hold, for a flat fee of 12,000 DZD / 80 euros. Excess fees vary by route (tariff PDFs on the site).

Conditions: extra baggage is subject to availability, may be limited for security reasons, cannot be transferred to another passenger or flight, and cannot be bought for infants under 2.

523.title: Air Algérie – Allowance and excess bag
523.text: Air Algérie – Additional and excess baggage. Additional baggage: if your bags exceed the allowed number or size, or you want to bring extra bags, you can add pieces on top of your free allowance. Rates are published in a separate PDF ('Tarifs'). International excess: a bag counts as excess when it is over 158 cm (length + width + depth) and over 23 kg. Overweight bags: bags over 23 kg and up to 32 kg are charged at the published rates. Bags over 32 kg are not accepted at check-in and must be sent as cargo (fret). Oversize bags: bags over 158 cm but not over 203 cm can be checked if they fit in the aircraft hold, for a flat fee of 12,000 DZD (about €80). Free allowance: see the Piece Concept page (1Pc / 2Pc of 23 kg each depending on route, class and loyalty status).

524.title: ARPCE – Service Universel des Communications Électroniques
524.text: ARPCE – Universal Service of electronic communications (Service Universel des Télécommunications, SUT). Page dated 11 October 2020. Purpose: to give every resident, regardless of location or social status, access to basic telecom services, especially internet access, at affordable prices. It is a public policy and land-planning tool promoting social cohesion by reducing disparities. Market forces alone cannot guarantee reasonable prices in remote areas operators find unprofitable to serve. Funding: licensed operators and authorisation holders pay an annual contribution of 3% based on annual turnover. The State can also contribute, with amounts set by the finance law. Legal evolution: - Law 2000-03 (2000): established universal service as a founding principle for opening the postal and telecom markets to competition. - Executive Decree 03-232 (2003): objectives including network access, continuity, reasonable pricing and specified quality of service. - Executive Decree 17-106 (2017): raised the minimum speed from 512 kbit/s to 1 Mbit/s and required public education institutions to be connected at at least 1 Mbit/s.

525.title: ARPCE – Service Universel des Communications Électroniques
525.text: specified quality of service. - Executive Decree 17-106 (2017): raised the minimum speed from 512 kbit/s to 1 Mbit/s and required public education institutions to be connected at at least 1 Mbit/s. - Law 18-04 (2018): created a multisector commission chaired by the minister to develop and manage the SUT and a support fund. - Executive Decree 18-246 (2018): objectives including emergency call routing, telephone service, fixed and mobile internet in uncovered areas at a minimum of 2 Mbit/s, interconnection of public education and health institutions, basic infrastructure, and support for ORSEC emergency plans. - Executive Decree 18-247 (2018): rules for managing the support fund; ARPCE and the ministry carry out ex-post checks on operators' compliance.

530.title: ARPCE – Service Universel de la Poste
530.text: ARPCE – Universal postal service (Service Universel de la Poste). Last updated 21 January 2021. Legal framework: Law No. 18-04 of 10 May 2018 defines the universal postal service as a minimum offer of basic postal and financial services, of specified quality, available nationwide on a permanent basis at affordable rates. Executive Decree No. 18-246 of 9 October 2018 sets its content, the applicable tariffs and how it is financed. Content of the universal postal service: - Letter mail up to 2 kg, including books, catalogues and periodicals. - Registered mail (envois recommandés) and items with declared value. - Parcels (colis postaux) up to 20 kg. - Telegrams. - Mail for the visually impaired (cécogrammes). - Payment of pensions and social benefits. - Regular collection and delivery, including in sparsely populated or hard-to-reach areas. - Dedicated counters for people with specific needs. - Postal presence in all urban areas. Objectives: sustaining postal activity, universal access, continuity of the public postal service, affordable access to quality postal and financial services, better administrative, financial and service-quality performance, and security of deposited funds.

531.title: ARPCE – Service Universel de la Poste
531.text: of the public postal service, affordable access to quality postal and financial services, better administrative, financial and service-quality performance, and security of deposited funds. Financing: possible State funding set in the finance law; contributions from postal operators – 3% of pre-tax turnover for operators other than the universal service operator, and 3% of annual gross accounting profit for operators under the simple declaration regime. Related texts: Law No. 18-04; Executive Decree No. 18-247 on managing the universal postal and electronic communications support fund. The universal service operator is Algérie Poste.

In 2006 SNTF ordered 64 units for the Algiers suburban network; the first was delivered in 2010. Algiers ridership: 32.6 million passengers a year, about 91,000 a day, about 900 per train. Algiers suburban network: 26 stations served by electric units on three axes: - Alger – El Harrach: Alger, Agha, Ateliers, Hussein Dey, Caroubier, El Harrach. - West: Gué de Constantine to El Affroun, including Blida and Boufarik. - East: Oued Smar to Thénia, including Bab Ezzouar and Boumerdès. Distances: 54 km from Alger to Thénia; 68 km from Alger to El Affroun. Other cities: Constantine suburban network has 12 stations, Annaba 6 and Oran 9, with diesel services covering 50 km from Constantine, 15 km from Annaba and 38 km from Oran.

534.title: SNTF – Trains de grandes lignes
534.text: SNTF – Long-distance trains (grandes lignes). Page dated 18 February 2018. Fleet: trains pulled by GM-EMD diesel-electric locomotives with DEV INOX coaches. Service: SNTF offers 12 long-distance trains daily: - Algiers – Oran (round trip): 8 trains, 4 of them comfort class. - Algiers – Constantine (round trip): 2 trains. - Algiers – Annaba (round trip): 2 trains, with 1st- and 2nd-class couchettes and seated coaches. Refurbishment: coaches are being rehabilitated at the Sidi Bel Abbès rail maintenance workshops by an Algerian workforce; refurbished coaches get air conditioning, a passenger information system, power outlets and USB ports. New trains: in 2015 SNTF ordered 17 'Coradia Polyvalent' trains from Alstom (bi-mode diesel/electric, up to 160 km/h, 254 seats including 60 first class, PMR accessible) to serve Algiers, Constantine, Oran, Annaba and Béchar among others. Fares: round-trip tickets over 400 km get 20% off and are valid 2 months; youth (15–28) and senior cards give 20% off on journeys over 100 km; large-family card 30% off in 2nd class (see SNTF 'Avantages tarifaires').
